families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering.formal:
For every pairing of the antisymmetric sector, at every strength, feeding ratio and channel phase, the mass form evaluates in closed form:
\begin{equation}
H_{kl} \;=\; \cosh^{2}r\;\delta_{kl} \;+\; x(5+6x)\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},
\qquad
\mathrm{spec}\,H \;=\; \bigl(\cosh^{2}r,\ \cosh^{2}r,\ 1 + 6x + 6x^{2}\bigr),
\end{equation}
with $\bar{n}n^{\mathsf{T}} =: P_{[\bar{v}]}$ the projector onto the conjugate coherent ray, and the trace identity $\tr H = 3 + 8x + 6x^{2}$ tying it to the diagonal reading. Three clauses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Rank one plus floor.)} The normal-ordered form $\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle$ is exactly $2x(2+3x)\,P_{[\bar v]}$, rank one: one heavy family along the conjugate coherent ray with the light pair strictly massless. Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}'s texture is a theorem of the Gaussian freezing at operator level.
\item \emph{(The floor is the ordering shift.)} The entire mass-squared of the light pair is the symmetric-ordering term $\tfrac12\langle[\hat\Omega_{l}, \hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}]\rangle = \cosh^{2}r\,\delta_{kl} + x\,P_{[\bar v]}$ restricted to the light plane, exactly $\cosh^{2}r$: the ordering shift, evaluated at depth $r$; that this is the same half-per-mode structure that determines $\hbar$ in the series is a reading, with the series' ordering dictionary \cite[Thm.~5.7]{ButlerT9} as its locator, and not part of the proved content. The light families' masses are the ordering shift alone.
\item \emph{(The $S_{2}$ is unbreakable in the class.)} The spectrum depends on the pairing only through the depth $r$ (Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}); the channel phase and, at fixed $r$, the feeding ratio move only the coherent ray, and the light-pair degeneracy is exact for every pairing of the sector. Everywhere in the antisymmetric Gaussian class, $m_{e} = m_{\mu}$ identically: the $S_{2} \to 1$ stage of the cascade provably lies outside the Gaussian freezing.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (which reading of the $207$ is primary).} The store takes the reading used here, the eigenvalues of the face mass form $H$ as squared masses, as the primary dictionary for the charged-lepton ratio $m_{\mu}/m_{e} \approx 207$: in it the channel phase does not reach the spectrum of the source-built completions (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-stabiliser-to-z2}), and the $207$ is a property of the selected state, a population ratio of the two directions of the source's plane (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floor-plus-face-density}(iv)). The reading of the projected coherent face vector as the vector of square-root masses, the eigenvalues of a circulant whose channel phase carries the $207$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.koide-channel-phase-is-no-symmetry-angle}), is kept as a labelled alternative; it conflicts with the charged-lepton texture $c(\J + \delta_{c}E)$ that the neutrino paper's instances use with the breaking relation (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.theta23-at-s3-s2-direction}), which is not a circulant, and the two are not reconciled.

\emph{Note (the mass dictionary, provisional).} The eigenvalues of $H$ are read as the squares of \emph{pole} masses: the store's provisional dictionary assigns pole masses to the face mass form, in either reading. So exact Koide at pole masses is a premise of that reading, not a consequence: the stored targets (the channel-phase window, the exclusion of $\tfrac29$, the pair-number threshold) are pole-mass statements, and at common-scale running masses, as at the freezing scale, the target ratio would be about $210.7$ rather than $206.77$ and the series would need a cancellation of the logarithmic QED correction of the kind Sumino proposes (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.koide-channel-phase-target-depends-on-mass-definition}). The dictionary may be revised; this note records the choice, and the clauses above do not depend on it.
families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering.technical:
For every antisymmetric pairing, at any strength, feeding ratio and channel phase, Wick's theorem with the Gaussian data gives the mass form in closed form, $H_{kl} = \cosh^{2}r\,\delta_{kl} + x(5 + 6x)\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l}$ with $x = \sinh^{2}r$, so $\mathrm{spec}\,H = (\cosh^{2}r, \cosh^{2}r, 1 + 6x + 6x^{2})$. Its normal-ordered part is $2x(2 + 3x)$ times the projector onto the conjugate coherent ray: rank one, one heavy family with the light pair strictly massless, so the democratic texture is a theorem of the Gaussian freezing at operator level.

The light pair's whole mass-squared is the symmetric-ordering term, exactly $\cosh^{2}r$ on the light plane; reading it as the series' ordering shift is an interpretation outside the proved content. Since the spectrum depends on the pairing only through $r$, the light-pair degeneracy is exact throughout the antisymmetric Gaussian class, so $m_{e} = m_{\mu}$ there identically and the $S_{2} \to 1$ stage lies outside the Gaussian freezing. Reading the eigenvalues of $H$ as squared masses is the store's primary dictionary for the muon-to-electron ratio; the square-root-mass circulant reading is a labelled alternative, in conflict with the charged-lepton texture of the neutrino paper. The masses are read as pole masses, provisionally, so exact Koide at pole masses is a premise of that reading.

proofs.main:
Write $\hat\Omega_{k} = \sum_{pq}\Theta_{k}[p,q]\,a_{p}a_{q}$ with $\Theta_{k} = \tfrac12(E_{k} \otimes \varepsilon)$ symmetric and real, and put $\omega_{k} = \langle\hat\Omega_{k}\rangle = \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}M)$. By Wick's theorem (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}), using the symmetry of $\Theta_{l}$ to merge the two $NN$ terms,
\[
\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle = 2\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Theta_{k}N\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}\bigr) + \bar\omega_{k}\omega_{l}, \qquad
\langle\hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\rangle = 2\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Theta_{l}(\mathbb{1}+N^{\mathsf{T}})\Theta_{k}(\mathbb{1}+N)\bigr) + \omega_{l}\bar\omega_{k},
\]
so that
\[
H_{kl} \;=\; \bar\omega_{k}\omega_{l} + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}) + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}) + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}N) + 2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}N\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}),
\]
four pieces. Insert the Gaussian data of Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}: $N = s^{2}\,\overline{R} \otimes \mathbb{1}$, $N^{\mathsf{T}} = s^{2}\,R \otimes \mathbb{1}$ with $R = \mathbb{1} - \bar{n}n^{\mathsf{T}}$, and $\omega_{k} = 2sc\,n_{k}$. Every trace factorises over the tensor product, with $\mathrm{tr}(\varepsilon\varepsilon) = -2$ on the spinor factor, and on the family factor the only identities needed are $E_{k}E_{l} = e_{l}e_{k}^{\mathsf{T}} - \delta_{kl}\mathbb{1}$ (from $\sum_{j}\varepsilon_{kij}\varepsilon_{ljm} = \delta_{km}\delta_{il} - \delta_{kl}\delta_{im}$), hence $\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}E_{l}) = -2\delta_{kl}$ and $\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}E_{l}X) = X_{kl} - \delta_{kl}\,\mathrm{tr}X$, and $n^{\mathsf{T}}E_{k}n = 0$ (antisymmetry). The pieces:
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}) &= \tfrac14\,\mathrm{tr}(E_{l}E_{k})\,\mathrm{tr}(\varepsilon\varepsilon) = \delta_{kl},\\
\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}) + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}N) &= -\tfrac{s^{2}}{2}\bigl[\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}E_{l}R) + \mathrm{tr}(E_{l}E_{k}\overline{R})\bigr]\\
&= -\tfrac{s^{2}}{2}\bigl[(R_{kl} - 2\delta_{kl}) + (\overline{R}_{lk} - 2\delta_{kl})\bigr] = s^{2}\delta_{kl} + s^{2}\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},\\
2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}N\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}) &= -s^{4}\,\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}\overline{R}E_{l}R)\\
&= -s^{4}\bigl[-2\delta_{kl} - (n_{l}\bar{n}_{k} - \delta_{kl}) - (\bar{n}_{k}n_{l} - \delta_{kl}) + (n^{\mathsf{T}}E_{k}n)(\bar{n}^{\mathsf{T}}E_{l}\bar{n})\bigr]\\
&= 2s^{4}\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},\\
\bar\omega_{k}\omega_{l} &= 4s^{2}c^{2}\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},
\end{align*}
using $\mathrm{tr}\,R = 2$, $\overline{R}_{lk} = R_{kl}$, and in the third line the expansion of $\overline{R} = \mathbb{1} - n\bar{n}^{\mathsf{T}}$ and $R = \mathbb{1} - \bar{n}n^{\mathsf{T}}$ into four traces. Summing, $H_{kl} = (1 + s^{2})\delta_{kl} + (s^{2} + 2s^{4} + 4s^{2}c^{2})\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l} = c^{2}\delta_{kl} + x(5 + 6x)\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l}$ with $c^{2} = 1 + x$, which is \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}; the heavy eigenvalue is $1 + x + 5x + 6x^{2}$ and the trace is $3(1+x) + 5x + 6x^{2}$. The normal-ordered form is the first and last pieces of $\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle$ alone, $2s^{4}\bar{n}_{k}n_{l} + 4s^{2}c^{2}\bar{n}_{k}n_{l} = 2x(2+3x)\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l}$, rank one, which is clause (1); the ordering term is the remainder, $c^{2}\delta_{kl} + x\bar{n}_{k}n_{l}$, whose restriction to the light plane is $c^{2}$, clause (2); and clause (3) is the statement that \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift} depends on the pairing only through $r$ and the ray $n$. The script evaluates the four pieces and their sum in exact cyclotomic arithmetic, from the Wick formula and the Gaussian data, at rational hyperbolic points $(s, c) = (\tfrac34, \tfrac54), (\tfrac{12}{5}, \tfrac{13}{5})$, feeding ratios $\lambda \in \{0, \tfrac34, \tfrac43\}$ (chosen so that $|a|$ is rational) and channel phases $e^{I_4\chi} \in \{1, \zeta, \zeta^{2}\}$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_4$ commutes with the tower vectors), and confirms each piece against its closed form and the total against \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}; the trace and eigenvalue identities are checked as rational-function identities in $x$.

families.slot-covariance-of-mass-law.formal:
\emph{Premise (slot covariance).} Let $Z = (Z^{1}, Z^{2}, Z^{3})$ be a three-spinor composite, $\beta(Z)$ its face vector and $M(Z)$ the family mass law, the Hermitian form on face space that the families paper reads as the family Yukawa form (Hypothesis \claimref{families.hyp-face-identification}). The law is covariant under the full slot mixing $U(3)$ of the three-spinor system (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder}):
\[
M(Z \cdot U) \;=\; \overline{R_{U}}\,M(Z)\,R_{U}^{\mathsf T}, \qquad R_{U} = \det(U)\,U^{-1}, \qquad U \in U(3),
\]
equivalently under the internal $U(2)$ of every pair of slots. It is a flavour symmetry of the law and not of the state: a given composite's face vector is not invariant, and selects the family that carries the mass.

\emph{What it is for.} For a family form sesquilinear in $\beta$ with constant coefficients and the face-wise diagonal $2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$, the premise forces the Gram square $M = 2\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}$, of rank one, exactly at $\Lambda = 0$ and for the bracket part at any $\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-covariance-forces-gram-square}); covariance under the permutations alone leaves a nine-dimensional affine freedom, including the face-wise form with three equal families at the democratic point.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if the family mass law, derived from the composite's structure, is not covariant under the slot $U(3)$, for example if it carries slot-dependent coefficients as the permutation-covariant forms of that theorem's clause (iii) do; the Gram square, and so the premise within the sesquilinear class, is refuted if three nonzero family masses are shown to be needed by the law at $\Lambda = 0$.
families.slot-covariance-of-mass-law.technical: The three conformal spinors of a three-spinor composite can be mixed among themselves by a $U(3)$, under which the face vector, the three pairwise mass brackets, transforms by the cofactor law. The premise is that the rule assigning the family mass table to a composite respects this mixing, as a symmetry of the law; a particular composite's face vector breaks it, and its direction picks out the massive family. Under the premise, a sesquilinear family form whose diagonal entries are the faces' own mass terms must be the rank-one Gram square of the face vector, so classically one family is massive. Without it, with only the permutations of the slots as symmetry, many forms remain, among them one with three equally heavy families. The premise would be refuted by a derivation of the mass law that depends on the slot frame, or by a need for three nonzero masses at tree level with $\Lambda = 0$.
families.slot-covariance-of-mass-law.lay: In this framework's working identification, each family of matter particles corresponds to one pair among the three basic parts of a composite, and the three parts can be continuously mixed into one another. This assumption says that the rule which assigns masses to the families treats all such mixtures alike, even though any actual composite picks out a direction and so breaks that symmetry. With the assumption, the mass table is forced into a form in which only one family is heavy, which is the pattern seen in nature at first approximation. Without it, the rule would also allow three equally heavy families.

families.source-term-linear-tilt-mass-fu.technical:
Writing the deformed bracket as $B_{\Lambda} = b + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\Omega_{\omega}$, with $b$ the flat mass bracket and $\Omega_{\omega}$ the composite's $\omega$-bracket (a length), the join's leading term expands as $2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} = 2|b|^{2} + \tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}\,\mathrm{Re}(\bar{b}\,\Omega_{\omega}) + \tfrac{\Lambda^{2}}{18}|\Omega_{\omega}|^{2}$. The middle term is linear in $b$, its gradient at $b = 0$ is $\tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}\Omega_{\omega}$, nonzero if and only if $\Lambda\Omega_{\omega} \neq 0$, and at fixed moduli it is maximal when $\arg b = \arg\Omega_{\omega}$. This clause is proved.

At observation level, if the effective potential for $b$ is built on the mass functional with $b$ and the vacuum value of $\Omega_{\omega}$ treated as independent, the potential has a $\Lambda$-linear source and $b = 0$ is not an extremum unless the vacuum $\omega$-area vanishes; the phase of $b$ locks to that of $\Omega_{\omega}$ or its opposite, which is pure gauge. The condensate's value is reduced to the vacuum expectation of the $\omega$-area, which the framework defines but does not compute; the independence of the two variables is the assumption.
families.source-term-linear-tilt-mass-fu.lay: Expanding the formula for a particle's mass with the cosmological constant switched on reveals an extra term that is linear in the basic mass quantity. Such a term acts like a slope that pushes the system away from zero. So, if the energy landscape is built from this formula and the two brackets in it are treated as independent, a nonzero value cannot be avoided unless the vacuum value of one of them, the $\omega$-area, vanishes. The size of that value then depends on that one quantity, which the framework names but does not compute. This second step is a reading at observation level, and the independence of the two brackets is the assumption it rests on.

families.three-generations-faces-maximal.formal:
The maximal composite is three conformal spinors (twistors), a bound imported at observation level, and a massive matter unit is a two-spinor composite (Fact \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}). Given the bound, there are $\binom{3}{2} = 3$ ways to choose which two spinors of the maximal system carry the mass, each choice supplying an identical copy of the fermion content of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s}, its lepton doublet under Hypothesis (S). Conjecture: the three generations are the three two-spinor faces of the maximal three-spinor system. Corollary shape, at observation level: generation mixing is the overlap between distinct embeddings, a CKM-shaped structure with mixing angles set by the geometry of the faces.

\emph{Note (the face identification restated, 2026-11-01).} The identification is restated as three composites with separate slots: each face is its own two-spinor composite, with its own slot and pair modes, and the three are not subspaces of one slot space. Read in one state space with shared slots the faces are not three generations under one gauge group (\claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}): any Lie algebra acting linearly on the three slots leaves at most one face plane irreducible, so at most one face is a weak doublet, and the faces' chirality halves span $28$ states with one pair system shared by the faces, or $46$ to $47$ with separate pair modes, of the $48 = 3 \times 16$ that three generations need.

families.three-identical-families-mixing.formal:
Let the face-$F$ copy of the content be the composite of two conformal spinors (twistors) on the slots $F \subset \{1,2,3\}$, with the construction of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s} applied to it. Then the faces, three of them given the three-spinor bound of Fact \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}, carry identical fermion content whatever their number: the symmetric group $S_{3}$ of slot permutations acts transitively on the faces and carries the face-$F$ copy isomorphically onto the face-$\sigma(F)$ copy, so the three copies of $(2,3)$, and under Hypothesis (S) of $(2,3) \oplus (2,1)$, are isomorphic. Any two faces share exactly one spinor slot. At observation level, and flagged as such: inter-family mixing is therefore mediated by single-slot overlap, the structure of a mixing matrix with no vanishing entries and suppressed double transitions, the CKM shape. What remains conjectural is only the identification of the faces with the physical families; the multiplicity three (given the imported bound), the identity of the copies, and the intersection count are as stated.

\emph{Note (the face identification restated, 2026-11-01).} The identification is restated as three composites with separate slots: each face is its own two-spinor composite, with its own slot and pair modes, and the three are not subspaces of one slot space. Read in one state space with shared slots the faces are not three generations under one gauge group (\claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}): any Lie algebra acting linearly on the three slots leaves at most one face plane irreducible, so at most one face is a weak doublet, and the faces' chirality halves span $28$ states with one pair system shared by the faces, or $46$ to $47$ with separate pair modes, of the $48 = 3 \times 16$ that three generations need.

\emph{Note (the generation number, 2 November 2026).} Under the slot-module premise the number of generations, the number of separate composites, is free: the premise and anomaly freedom hold copy by copy for any number of them, and asymptotic freedom of both non-abelian factors, if it is required, allows one to five at one or two doublets (\claimref{synthesis.slot-module-makes-the-faces-separate-composites-and-leaves-the-generation-number-free}, clauses (3), (4)); the shared three-slot space fails the premise even for one face (clause (2) there), which complements \claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}. families.three-identical-families-mixing.technical:
A face is a two-element subset $F \subset \{1,2,3\}$ of the slots of the maximal three-spinor system, and the face-$F$ copy is the construction of one derived generation applied to the two-spinor composite on those slots. Because that construction refers only to its own two slots, a slot permutation $\sigma \in S_{3}$ carries the face-$F$ copy term by term onto the face-$\sigma(F)$ copy; as $S_{3}$ acts transitively on two-element subsets, all copies are isomorphic: copies of $(2,3)$, and under Hypothesis (S) of $(2,3) \oplus (2,1)$. Given the imported three-spinor bound there are $\binom{3}{2} = 3$ faces, and two distinct faces meet in exactly one slot, $|F \cap F'| = 1$.

At observation level only, this suggests that mixing between families is mediated by the shared slot, so that every entry of a mixing matrix is populated and double transitions are suppressed, the shape of the CKM matrix. No mixing matrix is defined, and the identification of faces with physical families remains a conjecture. (Note, 2026-11-01: the identification is restated as three composites with separate slots; in one shared slot space at most one face is a weak doublet under one gauge group and the faces' chirality halves span at most $47$ of the $48$ states three generations need, \claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}.) (Note, 2 November 2026: the number of generations is free under the slot-module premise and anomaly freedom, at most five if both non-abelian factors are to be asymptotically free; three is not derived, resting on the imported three-spinor bound and a family-symmetry reading, \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-makes-the-faces-separate-composites-and-leaves-the-generation-number-free}.)

families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail.formal:
On the principal series $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ with $\nu = m/H + O(H/m)$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) (Fact \claimref{families.imported-dictionary-exact-join}), so that $\mathrm{Im}\,w$ is the mass in Hubble units and, trivially,
\[
\mathrm{Im}\,w \;=\; \frac{m}{H} \;=\; N \cdot \frac{m}{M_{P}} .
\]
Under the rescaling of Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}, $\Lambda \to \kappa^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, the two factors have different status: $N \to N/\kappa$, which is the proved clause of Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}; and $m/M_{P}$ is invariant, $m$ fixed while $H \to \kappa H$, which is the observation-level reading of \cite[Prop.~7.6(1)]{ButlerT12} recorded in Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number} and is the premise of this proposition, so that the proposition stands at that level. Granting it, $\mathrm{Im}\,w \to \mathrm{Im}\,w/\kappa$, and consequently any relation $\mathrm{Im}\,w = f(N)$ that holds across the family of frozen points must satisfy $f(N/\kappa) = f(N)/\kappa$ for every $\kappa > 0$, which forces $f$ linear, $\mathrm{Im}\,w = cN$ with $c = m/M_{P}$ a rescaling invariant. A power law $\mathrm{Im}\,w \sim N^{a}$ with $a \neq 1$, the hadronic $N^{2/3}$ of Observation \claimref{families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-result} or any other clean exponent, is the relation $m/M_{P} \sim N^{a - 1}$ between two independent continuous moduli of the kinematic layer, which by Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number} fixes neither. So no kinematic attack can give an exponent other than one, and the exponent one says only that $m/M_{P}$ is a number. The Zel'dovich-Weinberg coincidence, $m_{h}^{3} \sim M_{P}^{2}H$, is $m_{h}/M_{P} \sim N^{-1/3}$ and can be, in this framework, only a coincidence of the present epoch or a dynamical relation among couplings, never a kinematic theorem. The map of failed routes in Observation \claimref{families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-result} is thereby closed by a proof rather than left open: the absolute scale dissolves into three separately assigned pieces, $N$ (the cosmological constant, behind the promotion decision and then the descent measure, the Standard-Model paper's successor (5)), the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2 \times 10^{-17}$ (a second rescaling-invariant modulus, the Standard-Model paper's successor (1), so kinematically not a function of $N$), and the Yukawa pattern, $y_{e} \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$ and the ratios (the section “The weight spectrum: the order of operations”). Only the third has computable structure available; and the second-order breaking and the CKM angles, being ratios and angles, are invariant under the rescaling and independent of the first two, so they depend on the third alone.
families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail.technical:
On the principal series $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$), the imaginary weight is the mass in Hubble units, $\mathrm{Im}\,w = m/H = N\,(m/M_{P})$ with $N = M_{P}/H$. Under the rescaling $\Lambda \to \kappa^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, $N \to N/\kappa$ (a proved clause), while $m/M_{P}$ is invariant (an observation-level premise, at whose level the result stands). Granting it, any relation $\mathrm{Im}\,w = f(N)$ valid across the frozen points must satisfy $f(N/\kappa) = f(N)/\kappa$ for every $\kappa > 0$, which forces $f(N) = cN$ with $c = m/M_{P}$.

So a power law $\mathrm{Im}\,w \sim N^{a}$ with $a \neq 1$, such as the hadronic $N^{2/3}$ or the Zel'dovich-Weinberg $m_{h}/M_{P} \sim N^{-1/3}$, relates two independent moduli and cannot be a kinematic theorem. The absolute scale splits into three separately assigned pieces: $N$, the rung unit $v/M_{P}$, and the Yukawa pattern; only the last has computable structure, and the rescaling-invariant breaking and CKM angles depend on it alone.
families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail.lay: Particle masses are tiny next to the Planck mass yet enormous next to the expansion rate of the universe, which invites guesses that a mass is some power of one large cosmological number. Granting that masses stay fixed when the cosmological constant is rescaled, a premise held at observation level, this result shows that any such relation must be a plain proportionality, which says nothing new. So no purely kinematic argument could have found a different power, and the old coincidence linking the pion mass to cosmology can, in this framework, only be an accident of the present epoch or a dynamical effect.

standard-model.coefficient-cannot-come-f.formal: No polynomial in the frozen point and its lifts produces the $126$ doublet direction, so the Georgi-Jarlskog coefficient cannot be derived from the transported frozen point alone, however many rungs it is lifted through: the lifts add rung vectors, and rung vectors wedge to grade at most one per rung, never to the pair-sector bivector. The mass mechanism can produce the coefficient only if the pair sector enters it, through $\sum_{i}v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$, which is the $B - L$ generator and, in the correspondence paper's language, the charge of the conformal spinor storey (the twistor storey). The weight programme's first deliverable is therefore restated more precisely once more: not ``a pair-number-dependent rung coupling'' in general, but specifically a coupling of the rung vector to the pair-sector $u(1)$ current, and the object in the series that already couples to that current is the mass bracket, whose direction Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-bracket-direction-charged-not} located in $120 \oplus 126$; its charge is wrong for a vev, but its $B - L$ structure is the right kind. Whether a neutral composite of bracket and rung vector reaches $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ is the next computation, and it is a computation, not a decision.
standard-model.coefficient-cannot-come-f.technical:

Since the symmetric doublet mass forms are spanned by the $10$ direction and $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$, the coefficient can arise only if the pair sector enters the mass mechanism through $\sum_{i} v_{i} \wedge w_{i}$, the $B - L$ generator.

standard-model.equal-weight-module.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), let $P = T^{\dagger}T + TT^{\dagger}$, the projector onto $
u^{c}$ and its conjugate built from the Majorana element $T$, and let $T^{u}_{\mathrm{GJ}} = v_{4}(B - L)\chi$ be the up-type $126$ direction. Keeping $v_{4}$ off the condensate, $v_{4} - (v_{4}P + Pv_{4})$, gives the mass form of $	frac34(v_{4} + T^{u}_{\mathrm{GJ}})$: the $10$ and the $126$ doublet at equal weight, coupling $(Q, u^{c})$ exactly as $v_{4}$ does and with no $(L, 
u^{c})$ entry; the same operation leaves the mass form of $w_{4}$ unchanged.

Moreover $a\,v_{4} + a'\,T^{u}_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ commutes with $P$ if and only if $a' = a$, which is exactly when it annihilates $

standard-model.family-no-go-vev-cannot-s.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), let the electroweak vev be a rung vector $x$ of the ten and let the families sit in a tensor factor $\C^{3}$ acted on by an arbitrary matrix $F$, so that $M_{e} = y_{e}F$ and $M_{d} = y_{d}F$ with $y_{e}$, $y_{d}$ the one-family Clebsches of $x$. The Yukawa pattern gives $|y_{e}| = |y_{d}|$, so $M_{e}$ and $M_{d}$ differ by a scalar of modulus one and have the same spectra in magnitude for every $F$.

Hence no structure in family space, the breaking $S_{3} \to S_{2} \to 1$ included, can give $m_{\mu} \neq m_{s}$ or $m_{e} \neq m_{d}$ at tree level; in the same way the Dirac neutrino matrix cannot be separated from $M_{u}$.
standard-model.family-no-go-vev-cannot-s.lay: In the simplest unified picture, one Higgs field gives electrons and down quarks the same mass, and neutrinos and up quarks the same mass. Assuming the spinor slots behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), this theorem shows that, if the Higgs is a single vector of the framework's ten-dimensional space, no arrangement of the three families can undo that equality at the simplest level of the calculation. Since real muons and strange quarks differ in mass, something beyond a single such vector is needed.

The family factor is a tensor factor: $M_{e} = y_{e}\,F$ and $M_{d} = y_{d}\,F$ are the same matrix up to the scalar $y_{e}/y_{d}$ of modulus one, and the characteristic polynomial of $cF$ is $\det(\lambda - cF) = c^{3}\det(\lambda/c - F)$, whose roots are $c$ times those of $F$. The up-type statement is the same computation with $x = v_{4}$ on $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$.

standard-model.fits-record-level.formal:
Under Hypothesis (S), Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}, Premise (EW) and the $v_{R}$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}, fit with complex couplings, at $M_{I}$, the nine charged-fermion masses, $|V_{us}|$, $|V_{cb}|$, $|V_{ub}|$, the CKM phase, $m_{3}$, $m_{3}/m_{2}$ and the three lepton mixing angles (the record's values \cite{PDG2024}, run to $M_{I}$ in the Standard Model). Let $\Delta$ be the largest $|d\ln O/d\ln p|$ for $O = m_{3}$ and $O = m_{3}/m_{2}$ over the Lagrangian couplings $p$, with (EW) held exact. Representative fits:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lllll@{}}
\toprule
couplings & factor $3$ of the second family & largest $|M_{\nu}|$ entry & $m_{1}$ & $\Delta$ \\
\midrule
$10$s, $126$, $120$ & through mixing with the third & $0.04$ GeV & $0.03$ meV & $8$, $11$ \\
$10$s, $126$, $120$ & from the $126$'s second-family entry & $2.9$ GeV & $0.1$ meV & $46$, $96$ \\
one $10$, $126$, $120$ & from the $126$ & $4.0$ GeV & $4.9$ meV & $59$, $167$ \\
$10$s, $126$, no $120$ & from the $126$ & $2.2$ GeV & $1.7$ meV & $2400$, $6700$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Every row reproduces every one of the eighteen observables; none is a prediction, the couplings outnumbering the observables. When the $126$ supplies the second family's factor $3$ directly, the neutrino Dirac matrix keeps an entry of $2$ to $4$ GeV, whose seesaw contribution would naturally be of order $1$ eV, and the measured masses arise only from a cancellation among complex terms, tuned to about one part in $\Delta$. In the first row the $126$'s second-family entry supplies about a tenth of $m_{s}$, the splitting comes through mixing with the third family, carried by the $120$ and the $10$s, and nothing cancels; its $m_{1}$ lies below the neutrino paper's bound of about $0.1$ meV \cite{ButlerT15}.
standard-model.fits-record-level.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), the imported Clebsch structure with the seesaw, Premise (EW) and the triplet vev $v_{R}$ required by the neutrino sector, numerical fits with complex couplings at $M_{I}$ reproduce eighteen observables: the nine charged-fermion masses, $|V_{us}|$, $|V_{cb}|$, $|V_{ub}|$, the CKM phase, $m_{3}$, $m_{3}/m_{2}$ and the three lepton mixing angles. The tuning is measured by $\Delta$, the largest $|d\ln O/d\ln p|$ for $O = m_{3}$ and $O = m_{3}/m_{2}$ over the Lagrangian couplings $p$.

When the $126$ supplies the second family's factor $3$ directly, a neutrino Dirac entry of $2$ to $4$ GeV survives and the measured masses need a cancellation tuned to about one part in $\Delta$, with $\Delta$ from $46$ up to $6700$. When the factor instead comes through mixing with the third family, carried by the $120$ and the $10$s, nothing cancels ($\Delta = 8$, $11$) and $m_{1} \approx 0.03$ meV. None of the fits is a prediction, since the couplings outnumber the observables.
standard-model.fits-record-level.lay: Granting the slot-statistics hypothesis (S) and the equal-weight premise (EW), on the unified route the paper follows the masses and mixings of all known fermions can be fitted to the recorded values, but there are more adjustable couplings than measurements, so the fits predict nothing. What they show is which arrangements need delicate cancellations. If the factor of three for the second family comes directly from one ingredient, the neutrino masses come out right only through fine tuning; if it comes through mixing with the third family, no tuning is needed.

proofs.main: Record level. The fits were found by numerical minimisation; the script stores the four coupling sets of the table, recomputes every observable and $\Delta$ from them, prints them as RECORD lines, and checks, as floating-point controls, that each set reproduces the observables and that $\Delta$ is below $15$ in the first row, above $40$ in the second and third, and above $1000$ in the fourth. With real couplings, which cannot produce the CKM phase, no fit of the tuned rows was found with $f_{J} \le \sqrt{4\pi}$. The computation rests on \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}, which supplies the Dirac mass matrices at $M_{I}$ and the type-I seesaw, and on \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}, which supplies the triplet vev $v_{R}$ of the Majorana matrix $M_{R} = v_{R}f$. The fits also rest on \claimref{standard-model.premise-ew-equal-weight}, which fixes the neutrino's Dirac entry along the heavy family direction, $4w_{u}f_{33} = m_{t}$, held exact in $\Delta$, and on \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, which names the species whose masses are fitted.

standard-model.grade-three-georgi-jarlsk.formal: Under Hypothesis (S), $w_{4}(B - L)$ and $v_{4}(B - L)$ are pure grade three, so their forms lie in the $120$ component of $16 \otimes 16$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-spinor-bilinears}, with the equivariance of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}). Their mass forms on the sixteen are antisymmetric and couple exactly $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, respectively $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$, with lepton-to-quark modulus ratio $3$. With an antisymmetric family matrix the combined form is symmetric and vanishes on the family diagonal: the direction contributes only to entries between different families.
standard-model.grade-three-georgi-jarlsk.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), the one-sided weightings $w_{4}(B - L)$ and $v_{4}(B - L)$ are pure grade three in the Clifford algebra of the ten, so their forms lie in the $120$ component of $16 \otimes 16$. Their mass forms on the sixteen are antisymmetric, couple exactly $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, respectively $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$, and have lepton-to-quark modulus ratio $3$, the Georgi-Jarlskog ratio.

Combined with an antisymmetric family matrix the total form is symmetric and vanishes on the family diagonal, so this direction contributes only to entries between different families.
standard-model.grade-three-georgi-jarlsk.lay: The factor of three that unified theories need between some lepton and quark masses can also come, assuming the slots behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), from a second kind of ingredient, built here from the same charge that tells quarks from leptons. This ingredient cannot give mass within a single family; it only links different families. That makes it a candidate for supplying the factor through mixing between the second and third families.

standard-model.no-go-frozen-point-lifts-.formal: Let $I$ be the frozen point, a vector of the first rung's hyperbolic plane inside the pair space $W \oplus \overline{W}$ (in mode terms $I = a\,v_{1} + b\,w_{1}$ with $Q(I) = ab$), and let $c_{4} = -w_{4} + \lambda v_{4}$ and $c_{5} = -w_{5}$ be the rung components of its two lifts (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}, $\lambda = \Lambda/3$). Then the unital associative algebra generated by $\{I, c_{4}, c_{5}\}$ is eight-dimensional, spanned by $1, I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}, Ic_{5}, c_{4}c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}$, its odd part is $\mathrm{span}\{I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}\}$, and of these $c_{4}$ and $c_{5}$ are grade one (the $10$) while $I$ and $Ic_{4}c_{5}$ carry a pair-mode index and are not colour singlets. The algebra contains no colour-singlet doublet direction beyond the $10$, hence not $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$; and the pair-sector $u(1)$ bivector $\sum_{i}v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$, the factor $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ needs, is not in it.
standard-model.no-go-frozen-point-lifts-.technical:
Let $I = a\,v_{1} + b\,w_{1}$ be the frozen point, with $Q(I) = ab$, and let $c_{4} = -w_{4} + \lambda v_{4}$ and $c_{5} = -w_{5}$ be the rung components of its two lifts, $\lambda = \Lambda/3$. The three generators square to scalars and pairwise anticommute, so the unital associative algebra they generate is eight-dimensional, spanned by $1, I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}, Ic_{5}, c_{4}c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}$.

Its odd part is spanned by $I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}$; only $c_{4}$ and $c_{5}$ are colour singlets, and they are grade-one vectors of the $10$. So the algebra contains no colour-singlet doublet direction beyond the $10$, in particular not $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$, and it does not contain the pair-sector bivector $\sum_{i} v_{i} \wedge w_{i}$ that $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ needs.
standard-model.no-go-frozen-point-lifts-.lay: The framework's frozen point and the copies of it carried to higher levels generate a small algebra of operators. This theorem lists that algebra completely and shows it contains only the ordinary Higgs-like directions, not the special direction needed for the factor of three between lepton and quark masses. The missing ingredient is tied to the charge that separates quarks from leptons, which the frozen point never touches.
standard-model.no-go-frozen-point-lifts-.typing_note: Added the families Proposition, which supplies T_GJ and its need for the pair-sector bivector, since the conclusion is stated against it. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: Each generator squares to a scalar: $I^{2} = Q(I) = ab$, $c_{4}^{2} = Q(c_{4}) = -\lambda$, $c_{5}^{2} = 0$; and they pairwise anticommute, since $I$ lies in the pair space and $c_{4}, c_{5}$ in two different rung planes, mutually orthogonal. A unital associative algebra generated by three pairwise-anticommuting elements with scalar squares is spanned by the $2^{3}$ ordered products of distinct generators, and the script computes that span's dimension as exactly eight on the module (the generic $\lambda = \tfrac17$, $a = 2$, $b = 3$; degenerate choices only lower it). The odd products are the four listed. Colour: the $\su(3)$ generator $v_{1}w_{2}$ has nonzero commutator with $I$ and with $Ic_{4}c_{5}$ (script), because each contains the mode-one operators $v_{1}, w_{1}$ once; $c_{4}, c_{5}$ commute with all of $\su(3)$ (script), and are vectors: $c_{5} = -w_{5}$ has hypercharge $-\tfrac12$, and $c_{4} = -w_{4} + \lambda v_{4}$ is a combination of the hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $+\tfrac12$ vectors $w_{4}, v_{4}$, not a hypercharge eigenvector for $\lambda \ne 0$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i)). The script also computes the $\su(3)$-invariant part of the odd span as a nullspace, finds it to be exactly $\mathrm{span}\{c_{4}, c_{5}\}$ inside the span of the ten mode operators, and finds $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ (\claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}) outside it and $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$'s mass form outside the span of that part's mass forms. Finally the script adjoins $\sum_{i}v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$ to the eight products and finds the rank rise to nine.

standard-model.space-symmetric-doublet-m.formal: Under Hypothesis (S), on the sixteen of one generation, the symmetric bilinear forms $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ with $T$ an odd colour-singlet element of the Clifford algebra of the ten carrying hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $T_{3} = -\tfrac12$ span exactly a two-dimensional space, spanned by the form of the $10$ direction $w_{4}$ (Clebsch ratio $|y_{e}/y_{d}| = 1$) and the form of $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ (ratio $3$). Every form in the space couples only $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, and the ratio $y_{e}/y_{d}$ takes every value as the two coefficients vary: the representation theory fixes the two directions and not the ratio.
standard-model.space-symmetric-doublet-m.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), consider the symmetric forms $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ on the sixteen of one generation, with $T$ an odd colour-singlet element of the Clifford algebra of the ten carrying hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $T_{3} = -\tfrac12$. They span exactly a two-dimensional space, with basis the $10$ form of $w_{4}$ (ratio $|y_{e}/y_{d}| = 1$) and the $126$ form of $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ (ratio $3$).

Every form in the space couples only $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, and the ratio $y_{e}/y_{d}$ takes every value as the two coefficients vary: representation theory fixes the two directions but not the ratio.
standard-model.space-symmetric-doublet-m.lay: Under the slot hypothesis (S), for one family of quarks and leptons, the paper counts every way a Higgs-like field of the right charges can give mass to electrons and down quarks together. Mixing them can produce any ratio, so the symmetry alone does not pick the observed one.

proofs.main: $16 \otimes 16 = 10_{s} \oplus 120_{a} \oplus 126_{s}$, and a symmetric form of the stated charges is a component of the $10$ or the $126$ along a $(1, 2)_{-1/2}$ direction under $S(U(2) \times U(3))$; the $10$ has one such direction (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are}) and the $126$, decomposing under $SU(5)$ as $1 \oplus \bar 5 \oplus 10 \oplus \overline{15} \oplus 45 \oplus \overline{50}$, has one, in the $\bar 5$ (the $45$ carries the conjugate doublet, the $\overline{50}$ none). The script does this without the representation theory: it enumerates all $512$ odd monomials in the ten mode operators, selects those of the stated weights under $Y$ and $T_{3}$, computes the $\su(3)$-invariant subspace of their span as a nullspace over the rationals, forms the symmetrised Yukawa form of each invariant direction on all $16 \times 16$ basis pairs, and finds the span of the forms to have rank exactly two, with the forms of $w_{4}$ and $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ (\claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}) both inside it and no species pair other than $(L, e^{c})$, $(Q, d^{c})$ (the species named by (S), \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) coupled by any of them; the sum of the two normalised forms sends $(L, e^{c})$ to zero and leaves $(Q, d^{c})$, exhibiting a third ratio.

standard-model.what-direction-made.formal: Under Hypothesis (S), on the sixteen, the pair number $N_{W}$ takes the values $1$ and $3$ on the two rung-odd species $Q$ and $L$ and the values $0$ and $2$ on the rung-even ones, so $B - L$ takes four values where the rung algebra distinguishes only two parities. Among the operators $w_{4}$, $w_{4}N_{W}$, $w_{4}\chi$ and $w_{4}N_{W}\chi$, the first two have the $10$ form ($w_{4}N_{W}$'s symmetric form is $\tfrac32$ times $w_{4}$'s), the third has vanishing symmetric form, and only the fourth has the $126$ form, $|y_{e}| = \tfrac32$, $|y_{d}| = \tfrac12$, with $f(T_{\mathrm{GJ}}) = -\tfrac23 f(w_{4}N_{W}\chi)$ exactly, since $T_{\mathrm{GJ}} = w_{4}\chi - \tfrac23 w_{4}N_{W}\chi$ and the first term's form vanishes. The $126$ direction is the pair number read through the rung parity; neither factor alone reaches it, and the pair number is outside every object of the mass mechanism derived in the series.

synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-st.formal:
Suppose the quark Dirac mass matrices carry the textures of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation} at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction with one-type second stages, $M_{q} = c_{q}\bigl(\J + \delta_{q}(E + X_{q})\bigr)$, $q = u, d$, each $X_{q}$ odd under $P_{12}$ and symmetric, antisymmetric or Hermitian with any complex coefficient, as Proposition \claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule} takes for the leptons. Work at that order, where each sector's light states are the left singular vectors of $B_{q} = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2/3 & x_{q} \\ y_{q} & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ and $|x_{q}| = |y_{q}|$ (ibid.\ (i); Proposition \claimref{synthesis.series-family-structures-give-no-lopsided-second-stage}(iii)). Let $x = m_{d}/m_{s}$, $y = m_{u}/m_{c}$, and let $\phi$ be the relative phase of the off-diagonal entries of $B_{u}B_{u}^{\dagger}$ and $B_{d}B_{d}^{\dagger}$, which no rephasing of the families or of either sector's right-handed fields changes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The Gatto-Sartori-Tonin relation and the Cabibbo element.)} In each sector $\tan^{2}\theta_{q} = m_{1q}/m_{2q}$: this is the stored relation $\sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1} = \tan^{2}\theta$ for $|x| = |y|$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule}(ii), and Proposition \claimref{synthesis.series-family-structures-give-no-lopsided-second-stage}(iv) for complex stages), read in the quark sectors, where it is the relation of Gatto, Sartori and Tonin \cite{GST1968} for the nearest-neighbour texture of Fritzsch \cite{Fritzsch1978} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-fritzsch-texture-cabibbo-formula}). With it
\[
|V_{us}|^{2} = \frac{x + y - 2\cos\phi\,\sqrt{xy}}{(1 + x)(1 + y)} ,
\]
the heavy-quark-limit formula of the Fritzsch texture (Fritzsch and Xing, 1999, who also find $\phi$ near $90^{\circ}$; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-fritzsch-texture-cabibbo-formula}); the formula and that phase are standard and transport-absent, and what is new here is that the store's one-type light-plane block is that texture. Real stages, in particular every real texture of the form the store uses for the leptons, have $\cos\phi = \pm1$. A lopsided block, $|y_{q}| \ne |x_{q}|$, does not obey the first relation.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Excluded phases.)} If $m_{s}/m_{d} \in [18, 22]$ and $m_{c}/m_{u} \in [440, 580]$, then $\cos\phi = 1, \tfrac12, -\tfrac12, -1$ give $|V_{us}| < 0.196$, $< 0.2163$, $> 0.2301$, $> 0.247$, all outside $W = (0.22176, 0.22705)$, the join of three standard deviations of the stored global-fit and direct values.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The selected phase.)} Every point of the windows with $|V_{us}| \in W$ has $\cos\phi \in (-0.42, 0.36)$, so $|\cos\phi| < \tfrac12$: the up-down phase is within $30^{\circ}$ of a quarter turn. The quarter turn lies inside that range: under the same windows $\cos\phi = 0$ gives $|V_{us}| \in (0.2111, 0.2350) \supset W$; at the central ratios of the $N_{f} = 2+1+1$ lattice averages (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-flag-2024-light-quark-mass-ratios}), $m_{s}/m_{d} = 19.94$, $m_{c}/m_{u} = 505$, it gives $|V_{us}| \in (0.22256, 0.22257)$, inside $W$, and at those of the $N_{f} = 2+1$ averages, $20.36$ and $496.2$, it gives $(0.22054, 0.22055)$, just below $W$.
\end{enumerate}
So, under this hypothesis, the families paper's Cabibbo pass (Proposition \claimref{families.faces-ordered-what-identification-requires-first}(2), $\tan\theta_{d} = \sqrt{m_{d}/m_{s}}$) is realised at the breaking lemma's order only with a non-real up-down relative phase within $30^{\circ}$ of a quarter turn: the up-sector angle enters in quadrature and the down-sector angle alone gives $\sin\theta_{d} \approx 0.2185$ at the central ratios. Among the five phases with rational cosine that a finite symmetry supplies, only the quarter turn is compatible, and only within the spread of the lattice averages; $\phi$ is one free number selected by one observable and $|V_{us}|$ is not predicted. The phase comes from couplings independent of each other in the two sectors' second stages (for the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion, the frame coefficients and the two family matrices $Y$, $\tilde{Y}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}), and nothing stored fixes it. The one-type hypothesis is what family-symmetric couplings supply: second stages built from the $10$s, among them that completion's $Y$ and $\tilde{Y}$, have $y_{s} = x_{s}$ in every sector (\claimref{synthesis.complex-neutrino-stages-keep-the-solar-sum-rule}, clause (v), where the same stages fail the solar angle under Premise (H)). Real one-type quark stages give no Cabibbo angle, which with Proposition \claimref{synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns} leaves the quark second stage two requirements: $S_{2}$-odd entries, and a relative phase between up and down within $30^{\circ}$ of a quarter turn.
synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-st.technical: Under the hypothesis of a one-type $S_{2}$-odd second stage in each quark sector, at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction, the light-plane block has $|x| = |y|$, its light state makes the angle $\theta$ with $\tan^{2}\theta = m_{\mathrm{light}}/m_{\mathrm{heavy}}$ (the stored light-plane relation, which in the quark sectors is the Gatto-Sartori-Tonin relation for the Fritzsch texture), and the Cabibbo element is $|V_{us}|^{2} = (x + y - 2\cos\phi\sqrt{xy})/((1 + x)(1 + y))$ with $x = m_{d}/m_{s}$, $y = m_{u}/m_{c}$ and $\phi$ the physical relative phase of the two sectors' stages. With the lattice ratios ($m_{s}/m_{d} \in [18, 22]$, $m_{c}/m_{u} \in [440, 580]$) real stages give $|V_{us}| < 0.196$ or $> 0.247$, and $\cos\phi = \pm\tfrac12$ give $< 0.2163$ or $> 0.2301$, all outside the measured window $(0.22176, 0.22705)$; the data need $|\cos\phi| < \tfrac12$, an up-down phase within $30^{\circ}$ of a quarter turn; the quarter turn itself gives $(0.2111, 0.2350)$ over the windows, $0.22257$ at the $N_{f} = 2+1+1$ central ratios and $0.22055$, just below the window, at the $N_{f} = 2+1$ ones. The store's real textures therefore give no Cabibbo angle. The phase is one free number fixed by one observable, not a prediction, and nothing stored fixes it; the formula and a phase near $90^{\circ}$ are standard results of the Fritzsch-texture literature. Certified rational arithmetic and exact Gaussian-rational instances.
synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-st.lay: A well-known pattern from the 1960s and 1970s says that the angle describing how the down and strange quarks mix is roughly the square root of the ratio of their masses. In this framework, the same mathematical block that governs the lightest two families of leptons, if it also governs the quarks, reproduces that pattern exactly. But the up-type quarks contribute too, and how their contribution combines depends on a relative phase between the up and down sectors. Using current lattice values of the quark mass ratios, the measured mixing is reached only if that phase is within about thirty degrees of a quarter turn; with no phase, as in the real mass patterns the framework has written down so far, the result is clearly wrong. The phase is a free number that the measurement selects, so this is not a prediction; of five simple phases a symmetry could provide, only the quarter turn is compatible, and only within the spread between lattice calculations.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The hypothesis puts each quark Dirac matrix in the form of the charged-lepton matrix of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule}, with its own $c_{q}$, $\delta_{q}$ and one-type $P_{12}$-odd $X_{q}$, at the order of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation}. Clause (i) of that proposition is a statement about every texture of this form: the light states are the left singular vectors of the compression $B_{q}$ of $E + X_{q}$ to the light plane, in the basis $(\hat{b}_{e}, \hat{b}_{o})$, $B_{q} = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2/3 & x_{q} \\ y_{q} & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, and for a Dirac sector the light masses are proportional to the singular values $\sigma_{1} > \sigma_{2}$. For complex one-type and Hermitian stages $|x_{q}| = |y_{q}|$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.series-family-structures-give-no-lopsided-second-stage}(iii)). The common factor $c_{q}$ and the heavy democratic state drop out of the light-plane overlaps. The mass ratios and $|V_{us}|$ are data; the ratio windows are hypotheses of (ii)-(iii), chosen to cover the lattice averages of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-flag-2024-light-quark-mass-ratios} by more than three standard deviations.

\emph{(i)} Write $H_{q} = B_{q}B_{q}^{\dagger} = \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} a & b \\ \bar{b} & d\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, $a = k^{2} + |x|^{2}$, $b = k\bar{y}$, $d = |y|^{2}$, $k = \tfrac23$. Read in the Pauli algebra $\Cl(3,0)$, whose paravectors $\mathrm{span}\{1, e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}\}$ are the $2 \times 2$ Hermitian matrices (the matrix trace being $2\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$), $H = \tfrac{a + d}{2} + h$ with the vector $h = \operatorname{Re}b\,e_{1} - \operatorname{Im}b\,e_{2} + \tfrac{a - d}{2}\,e_{3}$; its eigenprojectors are $\tfrac12(1 \pm \hat{h})$, $\hat{h} = h/|h|$ and the angle $\theta$ of the light state from the odd axis has $\cos 2\theta = (a - d)/(2|h|)$, $\sin 2\theta = |b|/|h|$. The eigenvalues are $\sigma_{1}^{2}$, $\sigma_{2}^{2}$ with $\sigma_{1}^{2} + \sigma_{2}^{2} = \operatorname{tr}H$ and $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2} = |\det B| = |x||y|$. The relation $\tan^{2}\theta = \sigma_{2}/\sigma_{1}$ is equivalent to $\cos 2\theta = (\sigma_{1} - \sigma_{2})/(\sigma_{1} + \sigma_{2})$, that is $\cos^{2}2\theta = (\operatorname{tr}H - 2\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2})/(\operatorname{tr}H + 2\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2})$ with $\cos 2\theta > 0$; for $|x| = |y|$ the left side is $((a - d)/2)^{2}/(((a - d)/2)^{2} + k^{2}|x|^{2})$ and the right side $(k^{2} + 2|x|^{2} - 2|x|^{2})/(k^{2} + 4|x|^{2})$ after the substitution $\operatorname{tr}H = k^{2} + 2|x|^{2}$, and $((a - d)/2)^{2} = k^{4}/4$, so both equal $k^{2}/(k^{2} + 4|x|^{2})$. This is the stored clause (ii) of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule} for $y = \pm x$ and clause (iv) of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.series-family-structures-give-no-lopsided-second-stage} for complex stages; the computation above only restates it in the form used below, and it is the relation of \cite{GST1968} for the texture of \cite{Fritzsch1978}. The check verifies the identity exactly on five Gaussian-rational $x$ (in $\mathbb{Q}(I_4)$, numbers being read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) with $y = \pm x$ and $y = \bar{x}$ (tabulated value $\cos^{2}2\theta = \tfrac{1}{46}$ at $x = y = 1 + 2I_4$), and that $y = 2x$ violates it. Hence $\sin^{2}\theta_{q} = m_{1q}/(m_{1q} + m_{2q})$.

The Cabibbo element is the overlap of the light up state with the second down state in the light plane: $|V_{us}|^{2} = \operatorname{tr}(P^{u}_{-}P^{d}_{+}) = \tfrac12(1 - \hat{h}_{u}\cdot\hat{h}_{d})$, and $h_{u}\cdot h_{d} = z_{u}z_{d} + \operatorname{Re}(b_{u}\bar{b}_{d})$, $z = (a - d)/2$, so $\hat{h}_{u}\cdot\hat{h}_{d} = \cos 2\theta_{u}\cos 2\theta_{d} + \sin 2\theta_{u}\sin 2\theta_{d}\cos\phi$ with $\phi = \arg b_{u} - \arg b_{d}$ (the check verifies the dot-product identity on four exact instances and that an imaginary $x_{u}$ against a real $x_{d}$ gives $\operatorname{Re}(b_{u}\bar{b}_{d}) = 0$, a quarter turn). Then $|V_{us}|^{2} = s_{u}^{2}c_{d}^{2} + c_{u}^{2}s_{d}^{2} - 2s_{u}c_{u}s_{d}c_{d}\cos\phi$, and with $s^{2} = t/(1 + t)$, $c^{2} = 1/(1 + t)$, $t = x$ or $y$, this is the displayed formula; it is the formula of Fritzsch and Xing (1999) in the heavy-quark limit (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-fritzsch-texture-cabibbo-formula}); the new step is only that the store's one-type light-plane block has that form. Invariance of $\phi$: a common rephasing $\operatorname{diag}(e^{I_4\beta_{1}}, e^{I_4\beta_{2}})$ of the left-handed family basis multiplies both $b_{u}$ and $b_{d}$ by $e^{I_4(\beta_{1} - \beta_{2})}$; a right-handed rephasing of one sector multiplies the columns of $B_{q}$ by phases and leaves $b = k\bar{y}$ unchanged, since $k$ and $y$ share the first column, and an overall phase of $c_{q}$ cancels in $H_{q}$. For real $X_{q}$, $b_{q}$ is real and $\cos\phi = \pm1$.

\emph{(ii)} For fixed $\cos\phi = c$ the numerator $x + y - 2c\sqrt{xy}$ and the denominator $(1 + x)(1 + y)$ are bounded separately over the boxes $x \in [\tfrac{1}{22}, \tfrac{1}{18}]$, $y \in [\tfrac{1}{580}, \tfrac{1}{440}]$ (each increasing in $x$ and $y$ apart from the $\sqrt{xy}$ term, which is bounded by its corner values), with $\sqrt{\cdot}$ by integer square roots at $10^{-30}$. This gives safe bounds: $|V_{us}| < 0.196$ at $c = 1$, $< 0.2163$ at $c = \tfrac12$, $> 0.2301$ at $c = -\tfrac12$, $> 0.247$ at $c = -1$. The window $W$ is $(0.22431 - 3 \times 0.00085, 0.22501 + 3 \times 0.00068)$ from the stored quantity and its note; all four bounds are outside it.

\emph{(iii)} The same bounds at $c = 0$ give $(0.2111, 0.2350)$, which contains $W$. At the central lattice ratios, $x_{0} = 2/(27.227 \times 1.465)$ and $y_{0} = 2 \times 0.465/(11.766 \times 27.227 \times 1.465)$, exactly, $|V_{us}|^{2}$ lies between $0.22256^{2}$ and $0.22257^{2}$. These central ratios are those of the $N_{f} = 2+1+1$ averages; at the $N_{f} = 2+1$ central ratios, $x_{3} = 2/(27.42 \times 1.485)$, $y_{3} = 2 \times 0.485/(11.82 \times 27.42 \times 1.485)$ ($m_{s}/m_{d} = 20.36$, $m_{c}/m_{u} = 496.2$), the check certifies $|V_{us}| \in (0.22054, 0.22055)$, below $W$; both points lie in the windows. So the quarter turn is compatible only within the spread of the lattice averages, and the certified content is the range of $\cos\phi$ below. (Computed in floating point, orientation only: the phase that reproduces the global-fit central value at the $N_{f} = 2+1+1$ central ratios is $\phi \approx 93^{\circ}$; the down sector alone gives $\sin\theta_{d} = 0.2185$.) Solving the formula for $\cos\phi = (x + y - |V_{us}|^{2}(1 + x)(1 + y))/(2\sqrt{xy})$ and bounding over the boxes and $W$ (numerator extremes at opposite corners, denominator at its least value for the safe direction) gives $\cos\phi \in (-0.42, 0.36)$. The check also confirms that the central ratios of the stored $M_{Z}$ running masses, $18.97$ and $487$, lie in the windows.

\emph{Reading.} The Cabibbo pass of Proposition \claimref{families.faces-ordered-what-identification-requires-first}(2) compares $\tan\theta_{d} = \sqrt{m_{d}/m_{s}}$ with $|V_{us}|$; at the order used here the down sector alone gives $\sin\theta_{d}$, and the measured value is reached through the up-sector term at a non-real $\phi$. Proposition \claimref{synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns} showed that couplings respecting the residual $S_{2}$ give $V_{us} = 0$, so a quark second stage must break $S_{2}$; this result adds that a one-type such stage reaches the measured $|V_{us}|$ only with an up-down relative phase within $30^{\circ}$ of a quarter turn. That phase is one free number selected by one observable. The five candidate phases with rational cosine were fixed before the comparison, so the quarter turn is the data's choice among them (look-elsewhere count $5$; chance of one fit about $0.3$, an estimate), not a prediction. Nothing stored fixes $\phi$: it is a combination of the phases of couplings that enter the two sectors' stages independently. The result says nothing about lopsided quark stages, about $V_{cb}$, $V_{ub}$ or the Jarlskog invariant (outside the light plane at this order), or about whether the quark sectors share the lepton textures. Transport-absent.

synthesis.channel-phase-invisible-to-axi.formal:
Let $\hat\Omega_{k}$ and the mass form $H(\psi)$ be as in Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift} and Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}, $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} = \sum_{k}\bar{c}_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$, and for a real orthogonal family matrix $R$ with $\det R = 1$ let $\hat{R}$ be the Fock unitary $a_{iA}^{\dagger} \mapsto \sum_{j}R_{ji}a_{jA}^{\dagger}$. Let $u' = (1,1,1)$, $f_{+} = (1, \zeta, \zeta^{-1})$, $\zeta = e^{2\pi I_4/3}$ (numbers, the components of family vectors and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_4$ commutes with the tower vectors), and let $v(\chi) = \kappa(u' + \lambda e^{I_4\chi}f_{+})$ be the coherent face vector of an antisymmetric pairing (Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}), $\chi$ its channel phase.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Axial rotations move only the phase.)} A rotation $R$ about $u'$ commutes with the cyclic family shift, fixes $u'$, and multiplies $f_{+}$ by a phase $e^{I_4\theta}$: $Rv(\chi) = v(\chi + \theta)$. It commutes with complex conjugation and with every $S_{3}$-equivariant real structure $\sigma_{x,y}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}, and $H(\hat{R}\psi) = RH(\psi)R^{\mathsf{T}}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Invisibility.)} Let $\psi[c]$ be any state built from the vacuum by a fixed polynomial in $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ or $\hat\Omega(\sigma_{x,y}c)^{\dagger}$ and in face words invariant under real rotations (such as $\sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}$ or $\sum_{k}(\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger})^{2}$), or evolved from the vacuum by a Hamiltonian built from these. Then $\psi[Rc] = \hat{R}\psi[c]$, so the spectrum of $H(\psi[v(\chi)])$ does not depend on $\chi$: the channel phase cannot set any ratio of mass-form eigenvalues.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What can see it; computed, exact.)} The word $\sum_{k}(\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger})^{3}$, invariant under the cyclic family shift but not under rotations about $u'$, gives different characteristic polynomials of $H$ at $c$ and $Rc$ for rational rotations $R$ about $u'$, and equal ones at $c$ and its cyclic shift.
\end{enumerate}
So, if the charged masses are eigenvalues of the face mass form, the phase $\delta = 0.222$ of op.second-order-breaking (the channel phase in the real-slice reading of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(iii)) can only be produced by an interaction that sees the family basis beyond rotation-invariant data, reducing the axial $SO(2)$ to the cyclic shift, under which $\chi$ matters modulo $2\pi/3$. In the real-slice reading the masses depend on $\delta$ directly; the two readings are therefore not interchangeable.
synthesis.channel-phase-invisible-to-axi.technical: In the families paper the coherent face vector of every pairing is $\kappa(u' + \lambda e^{I_4\chi}f_{+})$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$): a democratic part, a Fourier doublet part of relative size $\lambda$ and a channel phase $\chi$, and in the real-slice reading of the charged spectrum $\chi$ is the Koide phase. Rotations of family space about the democratic axis fix $u'$ and multiply the Fourier vector $f_{+}$ by a phase, so they shift $\chi$ and nothing else. The mass form transforms covariantly under family rotations, and every construction that uses only the source, its complex conjugate or one of the store's $S_{3}$-equivariant real structures, plus rotation-invariant face words, commutes with these rotations. The eigenvalues of the mass form therefore cannot depend on $\chi$ for any such completion. The exact six-mode check confirms this for all four real structures and finds that a cubic family word, which sees the family basis, does respond to the rotation while still ignoring the cyclic shift. A completion that wants the observed phase to matter for the masses read as mass-form eigenvalues must contain structure of that kind.
synthesis.channel-phase-invisible-to-axi.lay: In the framework the three charged lepton masses are tied to a single angle, measured at about $0.222$ radians, and the open problem is to derive it. This result shows a restriction on where it can come from. The angle describes how a certain internal vector sits relative to a fixed axis; turning the internal space around that axis changes only the angle. Any mechanism that treats all such turns alike, which covers every mechanism built from that internal vector, its mirror image, the framework's notions of which directions count as real, and rotation-invariant combinations, therefore produces masses that cannot depend on the angle at all. Only a mechanism that singles out the three generations as a definite set of directions, not just up to rotation, can make the angle matter; the framework's permutation symmetry of the generations is such a structure, and an example built from it does respond to the angle.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} A rotation $R$ about $u'$ commutes with the cyclic family shift $C$ (both are rotations about the same axis), so it preserves the eigenlines of $C$, which are $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\,u'$, $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\,f_{+}$ and $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\,f_{-}$ (eigenvalues $1$, $\zeta^{-1}$, $\zeta$, distinct); being unitary it multiplies $f_{+}$ by a phase $e^{I_4\theta}$, and $Ru' = u'$. Hence $Rv(\chi) = \kappa(u' + \lambda e^{I_4(\chi + \theta)}f_{+}) = v(\chi + \theta)$, and as $R$ ranges over the rotations about $u'$, $\theta$ ranges over all angles. $R$ is real, so $R\bar{c} = \overline{Rc}$; it fixes $u'$ and is orthogonal, so it commutes with $P_{s} = \J/3$ and $P_{d} = 1 - P_{s}$, hence with $\sigma_{x,y} = (xP_{s} + yP_{d}) \circ \overline{\phantom{v}}$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(i)). For the covariance, $\hat{R}a_{iA}\hat{R}^{\dagger} = \sum_{j}R_{ji}a_{jA}$, and the cofactor identity $\sum_{ij}\epsilon_{kij}R_{i'i}R_{j'j} = \sum_{m}\epsilon_{mi'j'}\,(\det R)\,(R^{-1})^{\mathsf{T}}_{mk} = \sum_{m}\epsilon_{mi'j'}R_{mk}$ (for $R \in SO(3)$) gives $\hat{R}\hat\Omega_{k}\hat{R}^{\dagger} = \sum_{m}R_{mk}\hat\Omega_{m}$ for the face operators of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}; so $\hat{R}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\hat{R} = \sum_{m}R_{lm}\hat\Omega_{m}$ and, the mass form being $\tfrac12\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l} + \hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\rangle$ in every state (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}), $H(\hat{R}\psi) = RH(\psi)R^{\mathsf{T}}$, which has the spectrum of $H(\psi)$. Also $\hat{R}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat{R}^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(Rc)^{\dagger}$.

\emph{(ii)} By (i), $\hat{R}$ sends $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ and $\hat\Omega(\sigma_{x,y}c)^{\dagger}$ to the same operators at $Rc$, fixes rotation-invariant face words, and fixes the vacuum. So $\hat{R}\psi[c] = \psi[Rc]$ for every polynomial construction, and for evolutions under a Hamiltonian built from these operators, since $\hat{R}$ conjugates that Hamiltonian at $c$ into the one at $Rc$. Then $H(\psi[Rc]) = RH(\psi[c])R^{\mathsf{T}}$ has the same spectrum, and with $c = v(\chi)$, $Rc = v(\chi + \theta)$ for every $\theta$. The coherent vector's form is that of Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}. The check builds rational rotations about $u'$ by the Cayley transform $R = (1 - A)^{-1}(1 + A)$, $A = t[u']_{\times}$, at $t = \tfrac12$ and $t = -\tfrac27$, verifies $RR^{\mathsf{T}} = 1$, $Ru' = u'$, $RC = CR$ and $R \neq 1$, and for two complex-rational source vectors $c$ and all four $\sigma_{x,y}$ verifies $\sigma_{x,y}(Rc) = R\sigma_{x,y}(c)$ and that the states $\ket{0} + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\ket{0} + \tfrac23\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat\Omega(\sigma_{x,y}c)^{\dagger}\ket{0}$ at $c$ and at $Rc$ have normalised mass forms with identical characteristic polynomials, exactly.

\emph{(iii)} The check applies $\sum_{k}(\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger})^{3}$ (coefficient $\tfrac12$) to $\ket{0} + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\ket{0}$ and finds the characteristic polynomials at $c$ and $Rc$ different for both $R$ and both $c$, while at $c$ and $Cc$ they agree: the cyclic shift has $\det C = 1$, so $\hat{C}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat{C}^{\dagger}$ permutes the $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ and the cubic sum is invariant. A rotation-invariant quadratic sum such as $\sum_{k}(\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger})^{2}$ would not do, being invariant under all of $SO(3)$. Since the spectrum is a continuous function of $\chi$ and a cyclic-shift-invariant construction is invariant under $\chi \mapsto \chi + 2\pi/3$, such a construction can depend on $\chi$ only modulo $2\pi/3$. That $\delta = \chi$ or $\chi - \tfrac{\pi}{2}$ in the real-slice reading is Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(iii), where the projected vector depends on $\delta$ directly, which is why the two readings of the masses differ.
