synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-tu.formal:
Let $C(v) = \sum_{k} v_{k}^{2}$ be the bracket form on face space $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}^{3}$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_4$ commutes with the tower vectors, and the bar reverses $I_4$), $P_{s} = \J/3$ and $P_{d} = 1 - P_{s}$ the singlet and doublet projectors (Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}), $q(v) = s^{2} - Q(d)$ the equal-coefficient member of Proposition \claimref{families.koide-nullity-condition-one-member-invariant} for real $v$ with $s^{2} = C(P_{s}v)$ and $Q(d) = C(P_{d}v)$, and $\sigma_{x,y} = (xP_{s} + yP_{d}) \circ \overline{\phantom{v}}$ the $S_{3}$-equivariant real structures of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(i). For nonzero $a, b \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ put $D_{a,b} = aP_{s} + bP_{d}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The Lorentzian slice is a quarter-turn.)} The signatures $\pm(t^{2} - Q(d))$ on the slices of $\sigma_{1,-1}$ and $\sigma_{-1,1}$ are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(i), restated; what is added is their source. For $a, b \in \{1, I_4\}$, $\sigma_{x,y} = D_{a,b} \circ \overline{\phantom{v}} \circ D_{a,b}^{-1}$ with $x = a/\bar{a}$, $y = b/\bar{b}$, so the four $C$-compatible $S_{3}$-equivariant real structures are the conjugates of complex conjugation by $D_{a,b}$; and for real $v$, $C(D_{a,b}v) = a^{2}s^{2} + b^{2}Q(d)$. In particular $D_{1,I_4} = P_{s} + I_4 P_{d} = \exp(\tfrac{I_4\pi}{2}P_{d})$ carries the standard real face space onto the slice of $\sigma_{1,-1}$, and $C \circ D_{1,I_4} = q$ there. So $C$ has signature $(1,2)$ on the slice of $\sigma_{1,-1}$ exactly because that slice is the standard one read through $q$: the real structure and the choice of the light-cone member are one datum, the relative quarter-turn of the doublet.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The physical vector is null on no slice; a restatement.)} Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}(2) already gives $C(v_{\mathrm{lepton}}) = \sum_{k}m_{k} \neq 0$ and that $C$-nullity and $q$-nullity share nothing but the word; in the present terms: $C(v)$ is defined without reference to a real structure, and for a face vector with real components it is $\sum_{k}v_{k}^{2} > 0$. So the physical $\sqrt{m}$ face vector, with $C = \sum_{k}m_{k}$, is $C$-null on the slice of no $C$-compatible real structure; its quarter-turn $D_{1,I_4}v$ lies on the slice of $\sigma_{1,-1}$ and is $C$-null exactly when $q(v) = 0$, which is the Koide relation.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The angle is basis-free, and its Lorentzian form is a Lie real form.)} For Hermitian $A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_{k}$, $\operatorname{tr}A = \sum_{k}\lambda_{k}$ and $\operatorname{tr}A^{2} = \sum_{k}\lambda_{k}^{2}$, so $Q = \operatorname{tr}A^{2}/(\operatorname{tr}A)^{2}$ and $\cos^{2}\theta = (\operatorname{tr}A)^{2}/(3\operatorname{tr}A^{2})$ are the face-space data of the eigenvalue vector whatever the eigenbasis: $\theta$ is the Hilbert-Schmidt angle between $A$ and $1$. The map $A \mapsto \tfrac13(\operatorname{tr}A)1 + I_4 A_{0}$, with $A_{0}$ the traceless part, carries the Hermitian matrices onto $\R 1 \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3)$, the fixed set of the antilinear involutive Lie automorphism $X \mapsto -X^{\dagger} + \tfrac23\,\overline{\operatorname{tr}X}\,1$ of $\mathfrak{gl}(3, \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\})$; on it $\operatorname{tr}(X^{2})$ has signature $(1,8)$ (on the Hermitian matrices $(9,0)$), and its value on the image of $A$ is $\tfrac13(\operatorname{tr}A)^{2} - \operatorname{tr}A_{0}^{2}$, which is $q$ of the eigenvalue vector.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The root.)} Every positive semidefinite Hermitian $H$ is $A^{2}$ with $A$ Hermitian, with $2^{3}$ choices of $A$ when the spectrum is simple, and the Koide angle of $A$ depends on the choice. For the charged-lepton masses, with $m_{\tau} = 1776.93 \pm 0.09$ MeV as stored (Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data}) at its central value and both ends, the positive root gives $Q$ within $10^{-5}$ of $\tfrac23$, while every root with mixed signs gives $Q$ more than $\tfrac{3}{100}$ above it (the root with the electron's sign reversed gives $Q$ between $0.704$ and $0.705$).
\end{enumerate}
So the real-structure question of the families paper has a positive answer that carries no information: the Lorentzian slice exists, but choosing it is choosing the light-cone member, and the physical real vector is never on it. What would make the light-cone reading a consequence is a derivation of the quarter-turn $\exp(\tfrac{I_4\pi}{2}P_{d})$ from the series' structures. And since every positive semidefinite mass form is the square of a Hermitian face-space map, the Gram-square property as such has no content; the order-one angle fixes only that $\sqrt{m}$ is the spectrum of the positive square root, and a Gram-square premise with content must restrict the map, as the alignment proposition's rank-one square of the source does (Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(3)); a derivation of such a restriction from slot covariance is filed alongside, synthesis.slot-covariance-forces-gram-square.
synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-tu.technical:
Face space carries the complex bracket form $C(v) = \sum_{k}v_{k}^{2}$, which is Euclidean on real vectors, and the Koide relation is nullity for a different, Lorentzian form $q = s^{2} - Q(d)$ (singlet squared minus doublet squared). The store already shows a real structure of face space on whose slice $C$ is Lorentzian. This result shows why that is no progress: the slice is the ordinary real face space turned by a quarter-turn on the doublet, $D = P_{s} + I_4 P_{d}$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$), and $C$ pulled back by $D$ is exactly $q$. So the real structure and the light-cone choice are the same datum. Moreover $C$ of the physical face vector, whose components are the real $\sqrt{m_{k}}$, is $\sum_{k}m_{k}$ whatever real structure is chosen, so that vector is never $C$-null; only its quarter-turned image is, and exactly when Koide holds.

Two further facts. The Koide angle is the Hilbert-Schmidt angle between the square-root mass matrix $A$ and the identity, so it does not depend on the eigenbasis; and the light-cone form is the trace form of the real Lie algebra $\R 1 \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3)$ (signature $(1,8)$), onto which the same quarter-turn, applied to the traceless part, carries the Hermitian matrices. And any positive semidefinite mass form is the square of a Hermitian matrix, eight of them for a simple spectrum, with different Koide angles; for the charged leptons, at the stored tau mass, only the positive root gives $\tfrac23$ within $10^{-5}$ (the electron-flipped root gives a value between $0.704$ and $0.705$). So "the Yukawa form is a Gram square" says nothing by itself; the angle picks the positive root, and a Gram-square premise has content only if it restricts the map, as the rank-one square of the source does.
synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-tu.lay: The families paper notices that the Koide relation among the electron, muon and tau masses looks like a statement that a certain vector lies on a light cone, if lengths are measured in a relativistic way, and asks whether the framework's own geometry could force that way of measuring. This result shows that the obvious way to do it, choosing a different real section of the paper's complex space, is a relabelling: it amounts to rotating two of the three directions by a quarter turn, which is the same as choosing the relativistic measurement in the first place, and the actual vector of masses never lies on such a light cone without that rotation. A real explanation would have to produce the quarter turn from the theory. The result also notes that the paper's premise that the mass matrix is a square is automatic, and that what the measured angle really fixes is that the masses' square roots are all taken positive.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} $P_{s}$ and $P_{d}$ are real, symmetric, complementary projectors, so $D_{a,b}^{-1} = a^{-1}P_{s} + b^{-1}P_{d}$ and, for any $v$, $D_{a,b}\,\overline{D_{a,b}^{-1}v} = D_{a,b}(\bar{a}^{-1}P_{s}\bar{v} + \bar{b}^{-1}P_{d}\bar{v}) = (a/\bar{a})P_{s}\bar{v} + (b/\bar{b})P_{d}\bar{v} = \sigma_{a/\bar a,\,b/\bar b}\,v$. For $a, b \in \{1, I_4\}$ the ratios $a/\bar{a}$, $b/\bar{b}$ run over $\{1, -1\}$, and every pair $(x, y) \in \{\pm 1\}^{2}$ arises, which by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(i) are all the $C$-compatible $S_{3}$-equivariant real structures. For real $v$, $C(P_{s}v, P_{d}v) = v^{\mathsf{T}}P_{s}P_{d}v = 0$, so $C(D_{a,b}v) = a^{2}C(P_{s}v) + b^{2}C(P_{d}v) = a^{2}s^{2} + b^{2}Q(d)$, with $s^{2} = C(P_{s}v)$ the square of the singlet coordinate $s = v \cdot u$ of Proposition \claimref{families.koide-nullity-condition-one-member-invariant} and $Q(d) = C(P_{d}v)$ the Euclidean square of the doublet part. At $(a, b) = (1, I_4)$ this is $s^{2} - Q(d) = q(v)$. The slice of $\sigma_{1,-1} = D_{1,I_4}\,\overline{\phantom{v}}\,D_{1,I_4}^{-1}$ is $D_{1,I_4}(\R^{3})$, since $\sigma w = w$ if and only if $D_{1,I_4}^{-1}w$ is real. Finally $\exp(\tfrac{I_4\pi}{2}P_{d}) = P_{s} + e^{I_4\pi/2}P_{d}$ because $P_{d}$ is a projector. The check verifies the conjugation identity on real and complex test vectors for all four $(a, b)$, the pullback identity on seven real vectors, the signatures $(3,0)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(0,3)$ of $C$ on the four slices in the bases $D_{a,b}e_{k}$ by exact congruence (\texttt{GA.congruence\_signature}), and that $b = 1 + I_4$ makes $C$ non-real on the image (so the list is complete among quarter-turns).

\emph{(ii)} $C$ is a complex bilinear form on $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}^{3}$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$); a real structure only selects a real subspace. For $v \in \R^{3}$, $C(v) = \sum_{k}v_{k}^{2}$, which vanishes only at $v = 0$. The physical $\sqrt{m}$ face vector has real components $\sqrt{m_{k}} > 0$ (the reading of Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}(2), where $C(v_{\mathrm{lepton}}) = \sum_{k}m_{k}$), so it is $C$-null nowhere. By (i), $C(D_{1,I_4}v) = q(v)$, which vanishes if and only if the Koide relation holds (Proposition \claimref{families.koide-nullity-condition-one-member-invariant}), and $D_{1,I_4}v$ is fixed by $\sigma_{1,-1}$.

\emph{(iii)} Conjugation by a unitary preserves traces, so for $A = U\,\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,U^{\dagger}$, $\operatorname{tr}A = \sum\lambda_{k}$ and $\operatorname{tr}A^{2} = \sum\lambda_{k}^{2}$. For the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$, $s^{2} = (\sum\lambda_{k})^{2}/3$ and $s^{2} + Q(d) = \sum\lambda_{k}^{2}$, so $\cos^{2}\theta = s^{2}/(s^{2} + Q(d)) = (\operatorname{tr}A)^{2}/(3\operatorname{tr}A^{2})$, which is the squared cosine of the Hilbert-Schmidt angle between $A$ and $1$ (as $\langle A, 1\rangle = \operatorname{tr}A$ and $\langle 1, 1\rangle = 3$). Write $\Theta(X) = -X^{\dagger} + \tfrac23\,\overline{\operatorname{tr}X}\,1$. It is antilinear, and it is an involution: $\Theta(X)^{\dagger} = -X + \tfrac23(\operatorname{tr}X)1$ and $\operatorname{tr}\Theta(X) = -\overline{\operatorname{tr}X} + 2\overline{\operatorname{tr}X} = \overline{\operatorname{tr}X}$, so $\Theta(\Theta X) = X - \tfrac23(\operatorname{tr}X)1 + \tfrac23(\operatorname{tr}X)1 = X$. It is a Lie automorphism: $-[X,Y]^{\dagger} = [-X^{\dagger}, -Y^{\dagger}]$, and the trace terms are central and commutators are traceless. Its fixed set: on scalars $c1 \mapsto \bar{c}1$, fixed for $c$ real; on traceless $X$, $X \mapsto -X^{\dagger}$, fixed for $X$ anti-Hermitian; so the fixed set is $\R 1 \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3)$, a real Lie algebra of dimension $9$ whose complexification is $\mathfrak{gl}(3, \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\})$. For Hermitian $A$, the image $X = \tfrac13(\operatorname{tr}A)1 + I_4 A_{0}$ has real trace part and anti-Hermitian traceless part, so $\Theta X = X$, and $\operatorname{tr}X^{2} = \tfrac13(\operatorname{tr}A)^{2} + I_4^{2}\operatorname{tr}A_{0}^{2}$ because $\operatorname{tr}A_{0} = 0$; with $\operatorname{tr}A_{0}^{2} = \operatorname{tr}A^{2} - \tfrac13(\operatorname{tr}A)^{2} = Q(d)$ of the eigenvalue vector this is $s^{2} - Q(d)$. The check builds exact unitaries over $\mathbb{Q}(I_4) = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{Q}}\{1, I_4\}$ by the Cayley transform of two non-diagonal anti-Hermitian matrices, verifies these identities for three spectra each, verifies $\Theta^{2} = 1$ and the automorphism property on samples, and computes the signature of $\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on explicit real bases of the fixed set, $(1,8,0)$, and of the Hermitian matrices, $(9,0,0)$.

\emph{(iv)} A positive semidefinite Hermitian $H = U\,\mathrm{diag}(\mu)\,U^{\dagger}$ has the Hermitian square roots $U\,\mathrm{diag}(\pm\sqrt{\mu_{k}})\,U^{\dagger}$, eight when the $\mu_{k}$ are distinct and positive (and every Hermitian square root is of this form, since it commutes with $H$ and so preserves its one-dimensional eigenspaces), and $Q$ of a root is $\sum\mu_{k}/(\sum\pm\sqrt{\mu_{k}})^{2}$, which depends on the signs. The check exhibits this exactly for $\mu = (1, 16, 81)$, where the four values of $Q$ up to the overall sign are $\tfrac12$, $\tfrac{49}{72}$, $\tfrac{49}{18}$ and $\tfrac{49}{8}$. For the charged leptons, with $m_{e} = 0.51099895$ and $m_{\mu} = 105.6583755$ MeV (PDG central values, cited from memory) and $m_{\tau} = 1776.93 \pm 0.09$ MeV as stored in Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data}, rational bisection brackets each $\sqrt{m_{k}}$, and interval arithmetic at $m_{\tau} = 1776.84$, $1776.93$ and $1777.02$ gives $\lfloor 10^{6}Q \rfloor = 666659$, $666664$, $666669$ for the positive root, so $|Q - \tfrac23| < 10^{-5}$ there (computed, exact), and for the three mixed-sign roots values in $[0.704027, 0.704037)$, $[1.773009, 1.773073)$ and $[1.939436, 1.939517)$, each more than $\tfrac{3}{100}$ above $\tfrac23$. At the upper end of the tau range the positive root's $Q$ lies slightly above $\tfrac23$, as the stored Koide prediction $m_{\tau} = 1776.97$ MeV implies.

\emph{The closing paragraph} is argued from (i) to (iv), not proved: (i) and (ii) show that a real structure cannot by itself promote the light-cone reading, because the datum it adds is the quarter-turn and it leaves $C$ of the physical vector unchanged; (iv) shows that being the square of a Hermitian face-space map is automatic for a positive semidefinite mass form, so the content of the Gram-square premise lies in a restriction of the map, as in Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(3), where the leading form is the rank-one square $u'u'^{\mathsf{T}}$ of the source. Transport-absent: the statements are linear algebra on face space and on $3 \times 3$ Hermitian matrices.

synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-.formal:
Let $a_{iA}$ ($i = 1,2,3$ a family, $A = 1,2$ a slot) be the six bosonic face modes, $\hat\Omega_{k}$ the face operators and $H(\psi)$ the mass form of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}, evaluated in an arbitrary state $\psi$ as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}, and put $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} = \sum_{k}\bar{c}_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ for $c \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}^{3}$ (numbers, including the amplitudes of Fock states, and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_4$ commutes with the tower vectors, and the bar reverses $I_4$). For $U \in U(3)$ let $\hat{U}$ be the Fock unitary with $\hat{U}a_{iA}^{\dagger}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \sum_{j}U_{ji}a_{jA}^{\dagger}$, and $N(U) = \overline{\det U}\,U$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Covariance.)} For every state, $H(\hat{U}\psi) = N(U)\,H(\psi)\,N(U)^{\dagger}$, and $\hat{U}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(N(U)c)^{\dagger}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The stabiliser keeps the pair degenerate.)} Fix $c \neq 0$ and let $G_{c} = \{U : N(U)c = c\}$, which contains every $U$ fixing $c$ with $\det U = 1$ and so acts on $c^{\perp}$ as $SU(2)$. If $\hat{U}\psi = \psi$ for all $U \in G_{c}$, or only for two elements whose $N(U)$ have commutant $\mathrm{span}\{P_{c}, 1 - P_{c}\}$, then $H(\psi) = h_{c}P_{c} + h_{\perp}(1 - P_{c})$: $c$ is an eigenvector and the light pair is exactly degenerate. This holds for every such state, Gaussian or not, whatever its cumulants. It covers every state obtained from the vacuum by a polynomial in $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ and $U(3)$-invariant face words such as $\hat{V} = \sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}$, and every state evolved from the vacuum by a Hamiltonian built from $\hat\Omega(c)$, $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ and such words: one source and covariant interactions never split the pair.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Non-Gaussian instances; computed, exact.)} $(1 + (\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger})^{3})\ket{0}$ and $(\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger} + \tfrac13\hat{V}(\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger})^{2} + 2I_4\,\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger}\hat{V}(\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger})^{2})\ket{0}$ are invariant under $G_{e_{3}}$, have a nonzero ordered truncated four-point function $\langle a_{11}^{\dagger}a_{22}^{\dagger}a_{11}a_{22}\rangle^{T}$, so are not Gaussian (Wick's theorem, Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}), and have exactly degenerate light pairs with $h_{e_{3}} \neq h_{\perp}$; so does a state built from $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ and $\hat{V}$ on a complex $c$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Breaking it; computed, exact.)} Adding $(\hat\Omega_{1}^{\dagger})^{2}\ket{0}$ to the first state of (iii) splits the pair. Words that also use the complex-conjugate face vector, $\ket{0} + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\ket{0} + \tfrac23\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}\ket{0}$, which are covariant under real orthogonal $U$ only, split the pair for a complex $c$, generic or isotropic ($\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2} = 0$), and leave it degenerate for real $c$; the same words with $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ in place of $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ leave it degenerate.
\end{enumerate}
So the light-pair degeneracy of the skeleton is a symmetry statement about the source, not a property of the Gaussian class: a completion that splits the pair must carry a second face-space structure breaking $G_{c}$. A real structure on face space is one already in the store, and by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(ii) the coherent vector of every antisymmetric pairing with $\lambda > 0$ is not real up to phase under any $S_{3}$-equivariant real structure, which is the situation in which (iv) splits the pair. Whether a completion of that kind produces $m_{\mu}/m_{e}$ with no second free number is not decided here.
synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-.technical:
The families paper's Gaussian freezing leaves the electron and muon exactly degenerate, and the registered open problem asks for a non-Gaussian frozen vacuum that splits them. This result shows the degeneracy has a different cause, for every completion whose frozen vacuum keeps the symmetry of its one source. Family rotations act on the face operators through $N(U) = \overline{\det U}\,U$, and the mass form transforms covariantly, $H \mapsto NHN^{\dagger}$, in every state. A frozen vacuum built from one face vector $c$ (the source) and family-covariant operations is invariant under the rotations fixing $c$, which act on the two directions orthogonal to $c$ as $SU(2)$; by Schur's lemma the mass form is then a single number on that plane. That is true at every order of cumulants.

Exact six-mode Fock computations confirm it: invariant states with nonzero connected four-point functions have exactly degenerate light pairs, including states built with the covariant quartic word $\sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}$. Breaking the stabiliser splits the pair, and the store already supplies a way to do it: words that use the complex conjugate of the source, covariant only under real rotations, split the pair as soon as the source is not real up to phase, which every pairing with $\lambda > 0$ satisfies. The open problem therefore becomes: which second face-space structure, and whether it brings a free number.
synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-.lay: In the families paper, the electron and muon come out with exactly equal masses whenever the vacuum is of the simplest, Gaussian, type, and the paper's proposed way out was to use a more complicated vacuum. This result shows that complexity alone cannot work for any vacuum that keeps a certain symmetry. The equality is protected by that symmetry: the vacuum is built from a single preferred direction, and any rotation of the other two directions that leaves that one alone also leaves the vacuum alone. As long as that remains true, however complicated the vacuum, the two lighter particles stay equal. Exact computations confirm it. To separate them, some second ingredient must spoil the symmetry. One candidate already exists in the framework, a notion of which directions count as real, and with it the separation does appear in examples. Whether it gives the right ratio, about 207, is still open.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Since $\hat{U}$ is unitary with $\hat{U}a_{iA}^{\dagger}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \sum_{j}U_{ji}a_{jA}^{\dagger}$, taking adjoints gives $\hat{U}a_{iA}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \sum_{j}\bar{U}_{ji}a_{jA}$. The face operators are $\hat\Omega_{k} = \tfrac12\sum\epsilon_{kij}\epsilon_{AB}a_{iA}a_{jB}$ (Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}), so $\hat{U}\hat\Omega_{k}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \tfrac12\sum_{i'j'}\bigl(\sum_{ij}\epsilon_{kij}\bar{U}_{i'i}\bar{U}_{j'j}\bigr)\epsilon_{AB}a_{i'A}a_{j'B}$. The cofactor identity $\sum_{ij}\epsilon_{kij}X_{i'i}X_{j'j} = \sum_{m}\epsilon_{m i'j'}\,\mathrm{cof}(X)_{mk}$ with $\mathrm{cof}(X) = \det(X)\,(X^{-1})^{\mathsf{T}}$, applied to $X = \bar{U}$ with $\bar{U}^{-1} = U^{\mathsf{T}}$, gives $\mathrm{cof}(\bar{U}) = \overline{\det U}\,U = N(U)$, hence $\hat{U}\hat\Omega_{k}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \sum_{m}N_{mk}\hat\Omega_{m}$ and $\hat{U}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \sum_{m}\bar{N}_{mk}\hat\Omega_{m}^{\dagger}$. Therefore $\hat{U}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \sum_{m}\bigl(\sum_{k}\bar{N}_{mk}\bar{c}_{k}\bigr)\hat\Omega_{m}^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(Nc)^{\dagger}$, and $\hat{U}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\hat{U} = \sum_{m}\bar{N}_{lm}\hat\Omega_{m}$ (as $N$ is unitary), so
\[
H_{kl}(\hat{U}\psi) = \tfrac12\bigl\langle\hat{U}^{\dagger}(\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l} + \hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger})\hat{U}\bigr\rangle_{\psi} = \sum_{mn}N_{km}H_{mn}(\psi)\bar{N}_{ln} = (NHN^{\dagger})_{kl}.
\]
The check verifies both identities exactly on two generic states for four rational unitaries, two of determinant one and two not (a phase-diagonal times a Pythagorean rotation, and a permutation with a phase).

\emph{(ii)} If $\hat{U}\psi = \psi$ then by (i) $H = NHN^{\dagger}$, so $H$ commutes with $N(U)$. For $U$ with $Uc = c$ and $\det U = 1$, $N(U) = U$ fixes $c$, and on $c^{\perp}$ these $U$ form all of $SU(2)$, which acts irreducibly; so the commutant of $N(G_{c})$ is $\mathrm{span}\{P_{c}, 1 - P_{c}\}$ (the trivial character on $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\,c$ and the irreducible doublet on $c^{\perp}$ are inequivalent), and the Hermitian $H$ lies in it: $H = h_{c}P_{c} + h_{\perp}(1 - P_{c})$. Two elements suffice when their commutant is already this span, which the check confirms for the two used, by solving the linear equations $XN = NX$ over $\mathbb{Q}(I_4) = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{Q}}\{1, I_4\}$ and finding complex dimension $2$. For the covered states: by (i), $\hat{U}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat{U}^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ for $U \in G_{c}$; $\hat{V} = \sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}$ is invariant for every $U$ because $N$ is unitary; and $\hat{U}\ket{0} = \ket{0}$. So any polynomial in these applied to the vacuum is $G_{c}$-invariant, and so is the evolution of the vacuum under a Hamiltonian built from them, since the Hamiltonian commutes with every $\hat{U}$, $U \in G_{c}$. Mixed states that are averages of invariant states are covered by linearity of $H$ in the density matrix (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}).

\emph{(iii)} The check works in the six-mode Fock space with exact complex-rational amplitudes (in its code the families and the face index run over $0, 1, 2$, so $e_{3}$ is index $2$ and $a_{11}, a_{22}$ are modes $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$). For the two stated states it verifies $\hat{U}\psi = \psi$ for two non-commuting elements of $SU(2)$ on families $1, 2$ (both fix $e_{3}$ and have $N(U) = U$), that the normalised mass form is $\mathrm{diag}(h_{\perp}, h_{\perp}, h_{e_{3}})$ with $h_{e_{3}} \neq h_{\perp}$ (for the first state $h_{\perp} = \tfrac{361}{145}$, $h_{e_{3}} = \tfrac{461}{29}$), and that the discriminant of its characteristic polynomial vanishes. Both states have zero means, and the check computes the ordered truncated four-point function $\langle x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\rangle - \langle x_{1}x_{2}\rangle\langle x_{3}x_{4}\rangle - \langle x_{1}x_{3}\rangle\langle x_{2}x_{4}\rangle - \langle x_{1}x_{4}\rangle\langle x_{2}x_{3}\rangle$ for $(x_{1}, \ldots, x_{4}) = (a_{11}^{\dagger}, a_{22}^{\dagger}, a_{11}, a_{22})$ and finds it nonzero; for a zero-mean Gaussian state it vanishes by Wick's theorem (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}), so neither state is Gaussian. For the complex $c = (1, I_4, \tfrac12 + \tfrac{I_4}{3})$ the state $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + \tfrac23\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger 2} + \tfrac15\hat{V}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger 2})\ket{0}$ is checked invariant under two non-commuting products of reflections $1 - 2ww^{\dagger}/|w|^{2}$ in vectors $w \perp c$ (each of determinant one and fixing $c$), and its mass form is checked to act as one scalar on three vectors spanning $c^{\perp}$ and as a different scalar on $c$.

\emph{(iv)} For the four control states the check computes the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of the normalised mass form exactly: nonzero (three distinct eigenvalues, the light pair split) for the stabiliser-breaking state and for the real-structure words at $c = (1, I_4, \tfrac12 + \tfrac{I_4}{3})$ and at the isotropic $c = (1, I_4, 0)$; zero for the real-structure words at the real $c = (1, 2, -\tfrac12)$ and for the same words with $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ repeated in place of $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ at the complex $c$. Why: for real orthogonal $U$, $N(U) = \det(U)\,U$ is real, with $\det N = 1$, so $N\bar{c} = \overline{Nc}$ and the words are covariant under real rotations but not under $U(3)$. If $c$ is real up to a phase, $c = e^{I_4\phi}r$, then $\bar{c} = e^{-2I_4\phi}c$, the words are polynomials in $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ alone, and (ii) applies: the pair stays degenerate. If $c$ is not real up to phase, $\mathrm{Re}\,c$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,c$ are independent, a real $N$ with $Nc = c$ fixes both and so fixes a plane pointwise, and $N \in SO(3)$ is then the identity: no symmetry constrains the light block, and the computed instances split. The statement about the coherent vector is clause (ii) of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}: for $\lambda > 0$ no complex multiple of it lies in the fixed slice of any $S_{3}$-equivariant real structure.

synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-s.formal:
Let $Q(m) = \sum_{k}m_{k}/(\sum_{k}\sqrt{m_{k}})^{2}$ for positive $m = (m_{1}, m_{2}, m_{3})$ with $m_{3}$ the largest, the quotient of Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data}, and call $m' = (D_{1}m_{1}, D_{2}m_{2}, D_{3}m_{3})$ a dressing of $m$ by the factors $D_{k} > 0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Flavour-blind dressing.)} $Q(\lambda m) = Q(m)$ for every $\lambda > 0$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Dressing that favours the lighter flavours.)} If $D_{1}, D_{2} \ge D_{3}$ and $D_{j}m_{j} \le D_{3}m_{3}/9$ for $j = 1, 2$, then $Q(m') \le Q(m)$, with equality only when $D_{1} = D_{2} = D_{3}$. (With $s_{k} = \sqrt{m_{k}}$, $S_{1} = \sum s_{k}$, $S_{2} = \sum s_{k}^{2}$: $\partial Q/\partial s_{j} = 2(S_{1}s_{j} - S_{2})/S_{1}^{3}$, negative whenever $3s_{j} \le s_{3}$ and positive for $j = 3$.)
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The quarks.)} At the stored values ($m_{d}$, $m_{s}$ at $2$ GeV, $m_{b}(m_{b})$, $m_{t}$ direct) and at further standard definitions, $Q > \tfrac23$ in both quark sectors: down in $(0.731, 0.732)$ (stored) and $(0.745, 0.746)$ (running masses at $M_{Z}$); up in $(0.848, 0.849)$ ($m_{u}$ at $2$ GeV, $m_{c}(m_{c})$, $m_{t}$), $(0.831, 0.832)$ (charm pole mass) and $(0.888, 0.889)$ (at $M_{Z}$). So if the physical masses are a dressing of the kind in (i) or (ii) of brackets $m^{0}$, then $Q(m^{0}) \ge Q(m) > \tfrac23$: such a dressing cannot turn a Koide bracket ($Q = \tfrac23$) into the measured quark masses.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What a Koide bracket would need.)} If $D_{3}/D_{j} \le R$ for $j = 1, 2$ and $R\,m_{j} \le m_{3}/9$, then $Q(m^{0}) \ge Q(Rm_{1}, Rm_{2}, m_{3})$, which exceeds $\tfrac23$ for $R < R^{*}$ with $R^{*} \in (1.88, 1.89)$ for the stored down sector, $(2.19, 2.20)$ for the down sector at $M_{Z}$, $(8.67, 8.68)$ for the up sector at own scales and $(17.5, 17.6)$ at $M_{Z}$. A Koide bracket needs a dressing that enhances the heaviest quark over a lighter one by at least $R^{*}$. Neither (ii) nor (iv) treats a dressing that raises the middle mass and lowers the lightest relative to the heaviest ($D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$).
\end{enumerate}
Argued, not proved (standard QCD, cited from memory and not stored): perturbative strong dressing is of the kind in (i) and (ii): the mass anomalous dimension in a mass-independent scheme is the same for every flavour, so running between common scales is a common factor, and evaluating each mass at its own scale or converting to the pole mass enhances the lighter quarks, by asymptotic freedom; constituent dressing, additive and of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}$, favours the lighter quarks too. On that reading these dressings can only lower the quark quotients, and the quarks' failure of the relation is not produced by them from Koide brackets.
synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-s.technical: The selectivity account explains why Koide holds for the charged leptons and not for the quarks: leptons are undressed, quark masses are dressed by the strong interaction. This result tests that account and finds the dressing pushes the wrong way. The Koide quotient does not change when all three masses are multiplied by one factor, and it strictly decreases when the lighter masses are raised relative to the heaviest (as long as they stay below a ninth of it). Perturbative strong dressing is of this kind, by standard QCD (argued here, not stored): in the standard scheme all quark masses run by the same factor between common scales, and quoting each mass at its own scale, or as a pole mass, makes the lighter quarks relatively heavier. So the strong dressing can only lower the quotient. The measured quark quotients are above $\tfrac23$ in both sectors under every standard mass definition (between $0.731$ and $0.889$), so the undressed values would be further from Koide, not on it. A Koide relation at bracket level would need a dressing that favours the heaviest quark by a factor of at least $1.88$ in the down sector and $8.67$ in the up sector, which no known strong-interaction effect does.
synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-s.lay: A striking formula relates the masses of the electron, muon and tau, but it fails for the quarks. One proposed reason is that quarks feel the strong force, which changes their apparent masses, while leptons do not. This result checks the direction of that change. The formula's key number is unaffected when every mass is scaled by the same factor, and it goes down when the lighter particles get relatively heavier. The strong force does exactly that: it scales all quark masses alike, and where it differs it makes the lighter ones relatively heavier. So it can only move the quarks towards the formula from above, and the quarks sit above it already. The strong force cannot be what spoils the formula for quarks.

proofs.main:
Write $s_{k} = \sqrt{m_{k}}$, $S_{1} = \sum_{k}s_{k}$, $S_{2} = \sum_{k}s_{k}^{2}$, so $Q = S_{2}/S_{1}^{2}$, the quotient of Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data}.

\emph{(i)} $m \mapsto \lambda m$ sends $S_{2} \mapsto \lambda S_{2}$ and $S_{1} \mapsto \sqrt{\lambda}S_{1}$, so $Q$ is unchanged. The check confirms it exactly on rational square coordinates and confirms that a factor on one mass alone changes $Q$.

\emph{(ii)} $\partial Q/\partial s_{j} = (2s_{j}S_{1}^{2} - 2S_{1}S_{2})/S_{1}^{4} = 2(S_{1}s_{j} - S_{2})/S_{1}^{3}$; the check compares it with exact difference quotients. By Cauchy-Schwarz $S_{1}^{2} \le 3S_{2}$, and $S_{1} > s_{3}$, so $S_{2} \ge S_{1}^{2}/3 > S_{1}s_{3}/3$; hence $3s_{j} \le s_{3}$ gives $S_{1}s_{j} < S_{2}$ and $\partial Q/\partial s_{j} < 0$. For $j = 3$, $S_{2} = \sum s_{k}^{2} < s_{3}S_{1}$ since $s_{k} < s_{3}$ for $k \ne 3$ (or $\le$ with a strict term), so $\partial Q/\partial s_{3} > 0$. By (i) take $D_{3} = 1$. Along $t \mapsto (D_{1}^{t}m_{1}, D_{2}^{t}m_{2}, m_{3})$, $t \in [0,1]$, each light root rises monotonically to $\sqrt{D_{j}m_{j}} \le s_{3}/3$, so the condition $3s_{j}(t) \le s_{3}$ holds throughout and $dQ/dt = \sum_{j=1,2}(\tfrac12\ln D_{j})\,s_{j}(t)\,\partial Q/\partial s_{j} \le 0$, strictly unless $D_{1} = D_{2} = 1$. So $Q(m') \le Q(m)$. The check also confirms it on a rational grid of factors.

\emph{(iii)} The values (GeV): down stored $m_{d} = 0.00470$, $m_{s} = 0.0935$ (at $2$ GeV), $m_{b} = 4.18$ ($m_{b}(m_{b})$), from the stored quantities; up $m_{t} = 172.57$ (stored, direct measurements). Cited from memory and flagged: $m_{u} = 0.00216$ (at $2$ GeV), $m_{c}(m_{c}) = 1.273$, the charm pole mass $1.67$, and the running masses at $M_{Z}$, $(m_{u}, m_{c}, m_{t}) = (0.00127, 0.619, 171.7)$ and $(m_{d}, m_{s}, m_{b}) = (0.00290, 0.055, 2.89)$ (the 2008 table of Xing, Zhang and Zhou, Phys. Rev. D 77 (2008) 113016, recalled, not checked against the source). With certified rational bounds on every square root (integer square roots at $10^{-12}$), $3\sum m > 2(\sum\sqrt{m})^{2}$ holds in all five sets, with $Q \in (0.731, 0.732)$, $(0.745, 0.746)$, $(0.848, 0.849)$, $(0.831, 0.832)$, $(0.888, 0.889)$. If $m = D m^{0}$ with $D$ of kind (i), $Q(m^{0}) = Q(m)$; of kind (ii), $Q(m^{0}) \ge Q(m)$ by (ii) applied to $m^{0}$ (the hypothesis $D_{j}m^{0}_{j} \le D_{3}m^{0}_{3}/9$ is $m_{j} \le m_{3}/9$, true in every set). In both cases $Q(m^{0}) > \tfrac23$.

\emph{(iv)} $m^{0}_{k} = m_{k}/D_{k}$; by (i) rescale so that $m^{0} = (\rho_{1}m_{1}, \rho_{2}m_{2}, m_{3})$ with $\rho_{j} = D_{3}/D_{j} \le R$. By (ii) (its derivative statement, applied with the light factors moved up to $R$; the condition $Rm_{j} \le m_{3}/9$ is checked at the upper ends used) $Q(m^{0}) \ge Q(Rm_{1}, Rm_{2}, m_{3})$, whatever the $\rho_{j} \in (0, R]$. The check certifies $Q(R_{\mathrm{lo}}m_{1}, R_{\mathrm{lo}}m_{2}, m_{3}) > \tfrac23 > Q(R_{\mathrm{hi}}m_{1}, R_{\mathrm{hi}}m_{2}, m_{3})$ for the four stated brackets; $Q$ at the corner falls strictly with $R$, so $R^{*}$, its crossing of $\tfrac23$, lies between them (computed: $1.889$, $2.197$, $8.675$, $17.56$: $\sqrt{R^{*}}$ is the smaller root of $R(3p - 2a^{2}) - 4ab\sqrt{R} + m_{3} = 0$ with $a = s_{1} + s_{2}$, $b = s_{3}$, $p = m_{1} + m_{2}$).

\emph{The strong dressing (argued; standard QCD cited from memory, not stored).} In the MS-bar scheme the quark mass anomalous dimension depends on $\alpha_{s}$ and the number of active flavours but not on the flavour, and the decoupling at a heavy threshold rescales all lighter masses alike, so the running between two common scales is a factor of kind (i); this is why $Q$ at $M_{Z}$ is the bracket's $Q$ for any bracket defined at a common scale. Quoting each mass at its own scale $\mu_{k}$ increasing with $m_{k}$ multiplies it by $m(\mu_{k})/m(\mu_{0})$, which decreases with $\mu_{k}$ (asymptotic freedom), and the pole conversion $m_{\mathrm{pole}} = \bar m(\bar m)(1 + \tfrac{4}{3\pi}\alpha_{s}(\bar m) + \dots)$ has a positive correction decreasing with the mass: both favour the lighter quark, kind (ii) (the masses involved satisfy the ninth condition). Constituent dressing, of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ additive, favours the lighter quarks still more, and the top decays before it hadronises. So no strong dressing of these kinds can raise a Koide bracket to the measured quotients, and the selectivity account of Observation \claimref{families.selectivity-observation-level}, as far as it attributes the quark failure to the strong dressing, is excluded unless a dressing favouring the heaviest quark by at least $R^{*}$ is exhibited.

synthesis.mass-squared-reading-needs-mil.formal:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the span of face-word monomials and $H = (1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle)\mathbb{1} + G$, $G \ge 0$, $\mathrm{tr}\,H = 3 + 3\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle$, the mass form of a state on $\mathcal{S}$ as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floor-plus-face-density}, with eigenvalues $\lambda_{1} \le \lambda_{2} \le \lambda_{3}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every state on $\mathcal{S}$, pure or mixed,
\[
\frac{\lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3}}{\lambda_{1}} \;\le\; \frac{2 + \tfrac52\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle}{1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle},
\]
with equality exactly when $\lambda_{1}$ is the floor $1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle$ (as in every source-built state, loc. cit. (iii)).
\item[(ii)] If the state is supported on pair numbers $D \le K$, then $(\lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3})/\lambda_{1} \le 2K + 1 + \tfrac{2}{K + 2}$, with equality for the word $\hat\Omega_{1}^{\dagger K}\ket{0}$.
\item[(iii)] Under the mass-squared reading, $(\lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3})/\lambda_{1} = (m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2}$, which the stored pole masses place in $(12131147, 12138498)$ at three standard deviations (the face mass form gives pole masses under the dictionary the store adopts provisionally; at common-scale running masses the ratio is larger, \claimref{synthesis.koide-channel-phase-target-depends-on-mass-definition}, for the mass definition). So every state on $\mathcal{S}$ supported on $D \le 6065573$ is excluded, and the frozen vacuum must give positive weight to pair numbers $D \ge 6065574$; equivalently its moments must satisfy $\langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle + \tfrac52\langle\hat{D}\rangle + 2 > 12131147\,(1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle)$.
\end{enumerate}
So a selection rule for the non-Gaussian frozen vacuum that introduces no fitted number must, under the mass-squared reading, produce a pair-number scale of order $(m_{\tau}/m_{e})^{2}/2$ from structure; a rule confined to pair numbers below about six million cannot supply the charged-lepton masses on the span of face words, whatever state it selects there.
synthesis.mass-squared-reading-needs-mil.technical: On the span of face words the stored result writes the mass form as a floor $1 + \langle D\rangle/2$ times the identity plus a positive matrix, with trace $3 + 3\langle D\rangle + \langle D^{2}\rangle$, where $D$ is the number of face pairs. Since the least eigenvalue is at least the floor and the trace is fixed, the sum of the two heavier eigenvalues over the lightest is at most $(2 + \tfrac52\langle D\rangle + \langle D^{2}\rangle)/(1 + \tfrac12\langle D\rangle)$, for every state there, not only those built from the source. This is a ratio of two averages over the pair-number distribution, so over states supported on $D \le K$ it is largest at a single pair number $K$, where it equals $2K + 1 + 2/(K + 2)$. Reading the eigenvalues as squared pole masses, the measured $(m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2}$ is about $1.213 \times 10^{7}$, so the selected vacuum must put weight on pair numbers of at least $6065574$; at common-scale running masses the threshold is larger, an estimated $6.4$ million at first order in $\alpha$. A rule without a fitted number has to generate a number of that size.
synthesis.mass-squared-reading-needs-mil.lay: In one reading of the theory, the three charged-lepton masses squared are the three levels of a matrix built from the vacuum, and the vacuum is described by how many pairs of certain quanta it holds. This result shows that the ratio of the heavy levels to the light one can never exceed about twice the largest number of pairs present. Since the tau is about 3477 times heavier than the electron (at the pole masses), the squared ratio is about twelve million, so the vacuum must contain states with at least about six million pairs; with the masses defined at a common energy scale instead, the number rises to about 6.4 million. Whatever rule picks the vacuum has to produce a number that large from the theory's structure, without it being put in by hand.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} By Proposition \claimref{synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floor-plus-face-density}(ii), for every state supported on $\mathcal{S}$, pure or mixed, $H = f\mathbb{1} + G$ with $f = 1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle$ ($\hat{N} = 2\hat{D}$ on $\mathcal{S}$), $G \ge 0$, and $\mathrm{tr}\,H = 3 + 3\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle$. Expectations are taken in the normalised state; the pair-number distribution is $p_{D} \ge 0$, $\sum_{D}p_{D} = 1$.

\emph{(i)} Since $G \ge 0$, every eigenvalue of $H$ is at least $f > 0$; in particular $\lambda_{1} \ge f$. Then $(\lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3})/\lambda_{1} = \mathrm{tr}\,H/\lambda_{1} - 1 \le \mathrm{tr}\,H/f - 1 = (3 + 3\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle)/(1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle) - 1 = (2 + \tfrac52\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle)/(1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle)$, with equality exactly when $\lambda_{1} = f$. In every source-built state the forced eigenvector sits at the floor (loc. cit. (iii)), so there the bound is the stored identity for the heavier pair. The check confirms, on twelve random states with Gaussian-rational coefficients supported on $D \le 3$, the trace formula and $G \ge 0$ (all principal minors of the Hermitian $G$ nonnegative), computing $G$ from the monomial coefficients by the formula of loc. cit. (ii) in the auxiliary-boson form.

\emph{(ii)} Write $a(D) = 2 + \tfrac52 D + D^{2}$ and $b(D) = 1 + \tfrac12 D > 0$, so the bound of (i) is $\sum_{D}p_{D}a(D)/\sum_{D}p_{D}b(D)$. A ratio of two positive linear functionals of a probability vector is at most the largest of the ratios $a(D)/b(D)$ over the support (if $a(D) \le \rho\, b(D)$ for every $D$ in the support, summing with weights $p_{D}$ gives the same inequality for the averages). Now $a(D)/b(D) = 2D + 1 + 2/(D + 2)$, by direct division: $(D^{2} + \tfrac52 D + 2) = (\tfrac12 D + 1)(2D + 1) + 1$, and $1/(1 + \tfrac12 D) = 2/(D + 2)$. Its increment from $D$ to $D + 1$ is $2 - 2/((D + 2)(D + 3)) > 0$, so on $0 \le D \le K$ the largest value is at $D = K$. For the word $\hat\Omega_{1}^{\dagger K}\ket{0}$, $G$ is supported on the first direction ($\hat\Omega_{2}$ and $\hat\Omega_{3}$ annihilate it), so the floor is attained and the support is $\{K\}$: equality. The check verifies the division identity and the monotonicity for $D = 0, \dots, 60$, the inequality on the random states of (i), and equality at $K = 3$ ($\tfrac{37}{5}$).

\emph{(iii)} Under the mass-squared reading (the store's primary reading, as in loc. cit. (iv)) the eigenvalues are proportional to $m_{e}^{2}, m_{\mu}^{2}, m_{\tau}^{2}$ in increasing order, so $(\lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3})/\lambda_{1} = (m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2}$. With the stored masses and three stored standard deviations for the muon and the tau, and $10^{-9}$ MeV for the electron (covering its stored value and uncertainty), the check certifies in exact rationals that this ratio lies in $(12131147, 12138498)$, that $2K + 1 + 2/(K + 2)$ is below the lower end at $K = 6065573$ and not below it at $K = 6065574$. These are pole masses, which the store's provisional dictionary assigns to the face mass form. By (ii) and monotonicity, no state supported on $D \le 6065573$ reaches the measured ratio, so the frozen vacuum must give positive weight to some $D \ge 6065574$; by (i) its moments satisfy the stated inequality.

\emph{Scope.} The statement is about states on $\mathcal{S}$, which holds the Gaussian class and the source-built completions; it says nothing about states of the six face modes outside $\mathcal{S}$, and nothing in the $\sqrt{m}$ (circulant) reading, where the masses are not eigenvalues of $H$. No number is fitted: the inputs are the stored identity and the stored masses. It is transport-absent.

\emph{Mass definition (computed in floating point, not part of the check).} At common-scale MS-bar masses, from the pole masses by the one-loop QED relation (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-qed-pole-mass-relation}) with $\alpha$ between $1/138$ and $\alpha(M_{Z})$, $(m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2}$ is about $1.283 \times 10^{7}$ to $1.288 \times 10^{7}$ and the threshold about $6.41$ to $6.44$ million; the mass-definition dependence is treated in \claimref{synthesis.koide-channel-phase-target-depends-on-mass-definition}. If the selection rule fixes the mass form above the lepton thresholds, the running value is the relevant one; the conclusion that millions of pairs are needed does not depend on the choice.

synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floo.formal:
Let $a_{iA}$ ($i = 1, 2, 3$, $A = 1, 2$) be the six bosonic face modes of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift} (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}), $\hat\Omega_{k} = \tfrac12\varepsilon_{kij}\varepsilon_{AB}a_{iA}a_{jB}$ the face operators, $\hat\Omega(y) = \sum_{k}y_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}$, $\hat\rho_{lk} = \sum_{A}a_{lA}^{\dagger}a_{kA}$ the family density, $\hat{N}$ the number operator, $\hat{V} = \sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}$, and $H_{kl} = \tfrac12\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l} + \hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\rangle$ the mass form in an arbitrary state (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}). Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the closed span of the face-word monomials $\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} = \prod_{k}(\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger})^{m_{k}}\ket{0}$, $m \in \mathbb{N}^{3}$, $D = |m|$ (on which $\hat{N} = 2D$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Face-word algebra.)} The monomials are orthogonal, $\|\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0}\|^{2} = (D + 1)!\,m_{1}!\,m_{2}!\,m_{3}!$, and
\[
\hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} = (D + 1)\,m_{l}\,\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l})}\ket{0},\qquad
\hat\rho_{lk}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} = D\,\delta_{kl}\,\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} - m_{l}\,\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l} + e_{k})}\ket{0},
\]
so $\hat{V} = \hat{D}(\hat{D} + 1)$ on $\mathcal{S}$, $\hat{D} = \hat{N}/2$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Floor plus weighted density.)} For every state supported on $\mathcal{S}$, pure or mixed,
\[
H \;=\; \Bigl(1 + \frac{\langle\hat{N}\rangle}{4}\Bigr)\mathbb{1} + G, \qquad G_{kl} = \Bigl\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\,\frac{\hat{N} + 3}{\hat{N} + 2}\Bigr\rangle \ \ge 0,
\]
with $\bar{y}^{\mathsf T}Gy = 0$ exactly when $\hat\Omega(y)$ annihilates the state, and $\mathrm{tr}\,H = 3 + 3\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle$. So $H \ge (1 + \langle\hat{N}\rangle/4)\mathbb{1}$ on $\mathcal{S}$, the floor attained exactly on the face directions whose pair annihilator kills the state.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Source-built states: the ordering.)} In the normal frame of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-stabiliser-to-z2}, $c = (1, a, I_{4}a) = c_{R} + I_{4}c_{I}$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors), $a > 0$, $n = c_{R}\times c_{I}$, every state built from $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ and $\hat{V}$ on the vacuum (and every mixture of such) satisfies $\hat\Omega(n)\psi = 0$, hence
\[
Hn = \Bigl(1 + \frac{\langle\hat{N}\rangle}{4}\Bigr)n ,
\]
the least eigenvalue of $H$; $n$ is strictly the lowest exactly when the light pair is split, and the two heavier eigenvalues sum to $2 + \tfrac52\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle$. The observation recorded in that result (the forced eigenvector lowest in the source-built instances) holds for the whole class, and a word in $n$ itself is what can lift $n$ off the floor.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What a rule must fix.)} In a source-built state the lightest mass squared is fixed by the mean pair number alone, and the other two are the floor plus the eigenvalues $g_{\pm}$ of $G$ on $n^{\perp}$. Under the mass-squared reading, the measured charged-lepton masses require $g_{\mu}/g_{\tau} = (m_{\mu}^{2} - m_{e}^{2})/(m_{\tau}^{2} - m_{e}^{2}) \approx 3.536 \times 10^{-3}$ and $(\langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle + \tfrac32\langle\hat{D}\rangle)/(1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle) = (m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2} - 2$, so for a state of one pair number $D \approx 6.07 \times 10^{6}$ (arithmetic on measured masses, not checked; a dictionary and not a prediction).
\end{enumerate}
So on the span of face words, which contains the Gaussian class $\exp(\hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger})\ket{0}$ and the completions built from face words and $\hat{V}$ in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-stabiliser-to-z2}, the family splitting is the spectrum of a positive weighted density of face quanta above a floor set by the mean pair number; a rule selecting the non-Gaussian frozen vacuum must fix the pair-number moments and the population ratio of the two directions of the source's plane, and under the mass-squared reading the $207$ is that ratio.
synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floo.technical:
The face operators remove an antisymmetric pair of quanta from two different families, one per face. Applied repeatedly to the vacuum their adjoints build a subspace on which the algebra is simple: the monomials are orthogonal with known norms, each annihilator acts as the pair number plus one times a derivative with respect to the corresponding word, and the family density is not independent of the words. Putting these into the stored formula for the mass form gives a closed expression valid in every state of that subspace: the unit times one plus a quarter of the mean number of quanta, plus a positive Gram matrix, the one-body density of the face quanta weighted by a factor between one and three halves. The floor is reached in a face direction exactly when the state is annihilated by the pair operator of that direction.

For the frozen vacua built from the coherent source and its conjugate, the two words lie in the complex span of the source's real plane, and the pair annihilator along the normal of that plane differentiates each of them to zero. So the normal is an exact eigenvector at the floor, and it is the lowest; it is strictly the lowest whenever the electron and muon are split, and tied with a second direction only when the state is a single source. This turns the ordering observed in the stored instances into a theorem for the whole class and identifies what lifts the forced direction: only a word that uses that direction itself. The same formula gives the sum of the two heavier eigenvalues in terms of the first two moments of the pair number. In this class the electron's mass is fixed by the mean pair number, and the muon and tau by how the face quanta populate the two directions of the source's plane; under the mass-squared reading the measured spectrum fixes that population ratio and the second moment of the pair number, and a selection rule must produce both.
synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floo.lay: In the families paper the three charged leptons get their masses from a vacuum full of correlated pairs of quanta, and the electron and muon come out equal unless the vacuum is of a more complicated, non-Gaussian kind. Earlier work showed that symmetry alone cannot fix the electron-to-muon ratio and noticed, in computed examples, that one particular direction always came out lightest. This result explains why, and does so for every vacuum of the relevant kind. The mass formula turns out to have a simple shape: a common floor, set only by how many pairs the vacuum holds on average, plus a term that counts how the pairs are spread over the family directions. The direction that always came out lightest is one that, by construction, never receives any pairs in these vacua, so it sits exactly on the floor. The other two masses then measure how the pairs are shared between the remaining two directions. Reading the formula's eigenvalues as squared masses, as the families paper does, the famous ratio of about 207 becomes a statement about how a frozen vacuum shares its pairs, and any rule that chooses the vacuum must get that sharing right.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i) The algebra of face words.} The face operators are those of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}, and the modes are bosonic (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}). The commutator identity in the proof of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}, $[\hat\Omega(c), \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}] = 2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Theta\bar\Theta) + 4a^{\dagger}\Theta^{\dagger}\Theta a$, with $\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}\Theta_{l}) = \delta_{kl}$ and $4\Theta_{k}\Theta_{l} = \delta_{kl}\mathbb{1} - e_{l}e_{k}^{\mathsf T}\otimes\mathbb{1}$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cumulants-at-fixed-second-moments-keep-the-floor}, Step 1), reads, coefficient by coefficient in $\bar{c}_{k}c_{l}$,
\[
[\hat\Omega_{l}, \hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}] \;=\; (2 + \hat{N})\,\delta_{kl} - \hat\rho_{lk},
\qquad \hat\rho_{lk} = \textstyle\sum_{A}a_{lA}^{\dagger}a_{kA},
\]
while the $\hat\Omega_{k}$ commute among themselves, and so do the $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$. The density moves a family label: $[\hat\rho_{lk}, a_{jA}^{\dagger}] = \delta_{kj}a_{lA}^{\dagger}$, so with $\hat\Omega_{j}^{\dagger} = \tfrac12\varepsilon_{jab}\varepsilon_{AB}a_{aA}^{\dagger}a_{bB}^{\dagger}$ and $\varepsilon_{AB}a_{lA}^{\dagger}a_{bB}^{\dagger} = \sum_{m}\varepsilon_{mlb}\hat\Omega_{m}^{\dagger}$ (the pair is antisymmetric in $A, B$, hence in $l, b$),
\[
[\hat\rho_{lk}, \hat\Omega_{j}^{\dagger}] \;=\; \textstyle\sum_{b,m}\varepsilon_{jkb}\varepsilon_{mlb}\,\hat\Omega_{m}^{\dagger} \;=\; \delta_{kl}\hat\Omega_{j}^{\dagger} - \delta_{jl}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}.
\]
Since $\hat\rho_{lk}\ket{0} = 0$, $\hat\rho_{lk}$ acts on a monomial as a derivation: $\hat\rho_{lk}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} = \sum_{j}m_{j}(\delta_{kl}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m} - \delta_{jl}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{j})})\ket{0} = D\delta_{kl}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} - m_{l}\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l} + e_{k})}\ket{0}$. For $\hat\Omega_{l}$ induct on $D$: with $m = m' + e_{j}$ and the claim for $m'$ (degree $D - 1$, on which $\hat{N} = 2D - 2$),
\[
\hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{j}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'}\ket{0}
= \hat\Omega_{j}^{\dagger}\,D m'_{l}\,\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m' - e_{l})}\ket{0} + \bigl(2D\delta_{jl} - \hat\rho_{lj}\bigr)\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'}\ket{0}
= D m'_{l}\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l})}\ket{0} + 2D\delta_{jl}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'}\ket{0} - (D - 1)\delta_{jl}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'}\ket{0} + m'_{l}\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l})}\ket{0},
\]
which is $(D + 1)(m'_{l} + \delta_{jl})\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l})}\ket{0} = (D + 1)m_{l}\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l})}\ket{0}$, since $\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'} = \hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l})}$ when $j = l$. Then $\langle\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}0, \hat\Omega^{\dagger m''}0\rangle = \langle\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'}0, \hat\Omega_{j}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m''}0\rangle = (D + 1)m''_{j}\langle\hat\Omega^{\dagger m'}0, \hat\Omega^{\dagger(m'' - e_{j})}0\rangle$ for $|m''| = D$ (different degrees are orthogonal, being eigenvectors of $\hat{N}$), and induction gives orthogonality and $\|\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0}\|^{2} = (D + 1)m_{j}\cdot D!\,(m - e_{j})! = (D + 1)!\,m!$. Finally $\hat{V}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} = \sum_{k}(D + 1)m_{k}\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} = D(D + 1)\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0}$. The check verifies all of (i) entry by entry on the twenty monomials with $D \le 3$.

\emph{(ii) The mass form.} Comparing the formulas of (i) for $\hat\rho_{lk}$ and for $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}$ (which sends $\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0}$ to $(D + 1)m_{l}\hat\Omega^{\dagger(m - e_{l} + e_{k})}\ket{0}$) gives the operator identity on $\mathcal{S}$
\[
\hat\rho_{lk} \;=\; \hat{D}\,\delta_{kl} - \hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\,(\hat{D} + 1)^{-1}, \qquad \hat{D} = \hat{N}/2,
\]
$\hat{D}$ commuting with $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}$. The mass form is $H_{kl} = \tfrac12\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l} + \hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\rangle = \langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle + \tfrac12\langle[\hat\Omega_{l}, \hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}]\rangle$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}), so for a normalised $\psi \in \mathcal{S}$
\[
H_{kl} = \langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle + \delta_{kl} + \tfrac12\langle\hat{N}\rangle\delta_{kl} - \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle\delta_{kl} + \tfrac12\bigl\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}(\hat{D} + 1)^{-1}\bigr\rangle
= \Bigl(1 + \tfrac{\langle\hat{N}\rangle}{4}\Bigr)\delta_{kl} + \Bigl\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\,\frac{\hat{N} + 3}{\hat{N} + 2}\Bigr\rangle .
\]
Write $f = (\hat{N} + 3)/(\hat{N} + 2)$, positive and a function of $\hat{N}$; as $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}$ preserves $\hat{N}$, $G_{kl} = \langle\hat\Omega_{k}f^{1/2}\psi, \hat\Omega_{l}f^{1/2}\psi\rangle$, the Gram matrix of the vectors $\hat\Omega_{l}f^{1/2}\psi$, so $G \ge 0$ and $\bar{y}^{\mathsf T}Gy = \|\hat\Omega(y)f^{1/2}\psi\|^{2}$. Since $\hat\Omega(y)f(\hat{N})^{1/2} = f(\hat{N} + 2)^{1/2}\hat\Omega(y)$ and $f > 0$, this vanishes exactly when $\hat\Omega(y)\psi = 0$. Mixed states supported on $\mathcal{S}$ follow by linearity of $H$ in the density matrix. The trace: $\sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k} = \hat{V} = \hat{D}(\hat{D} + 1)$ on $\mathcal{S}$ by (i), so $\mathrm{tr}\,G = \langle\hat{D}(\hat{D} + 1)(2\hat{D} + 3)/(2\hat{D} + 2)\rangle = \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle + \tfrac32\langle\hat{D}\rangle$ and $\mathrm{tr}\,H = 3 + 3\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle$, in agreement with the trace identity $\mathrm{tr}\,H = 3 + \langle\hat{N}\rangle + \sum_{k}\|\hat\Omega_{k}\psi\|^{2}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cumulants-at-fixed-second-moments-keep-the-floor}. A reading, not used in the proof: the map $\hat\Omega^{\dagger m}\ket{0} \mapsto \sqrt{(D + 1)!}\,z^{\dagger m}\ket{0}$ is an isometry of $\mathcal{S}$ onto the Fock space of three auxiliary bosons $z_{k}$, under which $\hat\Omega_{l} = \sqrt{\hat{D} + 1}\,z_{l}$ and $G_{kl} = \langle z_{k}^{\dagger}z_{l}(\hat{D} + \tfrac32)\rangle$, the one-body density of the face quanta weighted by $\hat{D} + \tfrac32$. The check verifies the displayed formula for $H$ entry by entry, the trace identity and the Hermiticity and positivity of $G$ on five non-Gaussian superpositions of up to five monomials with complex rational coefficients.

\emph{(iii) Source-built states.} By (i), on $\mathcal{S}$ the operator $\hat\Omega_{l}$ acts on polynomials in the $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ applied to the vacuum as $(\hat{D} + 1)\,\partial/\partial\hat\Omega_{l}^{\dagger}$ (the factor taken at the degree acted on), so $\hat\Omega(n) = \sum_{l}n_{l}\hat\Omega_{l}$ acts as $(\hat{D} + 1)$ times the derivative along $n$. For $y \in \mathrm{span}_{\C}\{c_{R}, c_{I}\} = n^{\perp}$, the derivative of $\hat\Omega(y)^{\dagger} = \sum_{k}\bar{y}_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ along $n$ is $\sum_{k}n_{k}\bar{y}_{k} = 0$, since $n$ is real and orthogonal to $c_{R}$ and $c_{I}$; by the Leibniz rule the derivative of any polynomial in $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ and $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ (both in that span) vanishes, and $\hat{V}$ is a function of $\hat{D}$ on $\mathcal{S}$, so $\hat\Omega(n)\psi = 0$ for every state of the class, and for mixtures of such. By (ii), $Gn = 0$ and $Hn = (1 + \langle\hat{N}\rangle/4)n$, the least eigenvalue of $H$. The other two eigenvalues are $1 + \langle\hat{N}\rangle/4$ plus the eigenvalues of $G$ on $n^{\perp}$; if $G$ is singular there, both light eigenvalues equal the floor and the pair is degenerate (the single source, by (ii) exactly when $\hat\Omega(y)\psi = 0$ for some $y \in n^{\perp}$); otherwise $n$ is strictly the lowest and the pair is split. The trace identity of (ii) then gives $\lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3} = \mathrm{tr}\,H - \lambda_{1} = 2 + \tfrac52\langle\hat{D}\rangle + \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle$. The check works in the frame of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-stabiliser-to-z2} at $a = 1$ and $a = \tfrac23$, on seven states each (the truncated single source, the real family at $\beta = 1, 2, -\tfrac12$, the two-word state, and two states with $\hat{V}$ and degree-three words, complex coefficients): it verifies $\hat\Omega(n)\psi = 0$, $Hn = (1 + \langle\hat{D}\rangle/2)n$, and that the compression of $H - h_{n}$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive semidefinite (determinant $\ge 0$, trace $> 0$, in the basis $c_{R}, c_{I}$ with its Gram matrix), degenerate exactly for the single source; and it reproduces the stored values $h_{n} = \tfrac{32}{17}, \tfrac{145}{77}, \tfrac{505}{257}, \tfrac{55}{32}, \tfrac{190}{101}$ as $1 + \langle\hat{D}\rangle/2$ (for instance the real family at $\beta = 1$ has weights $1$, $16$, $60$ in degrees $0, 1, 2$, so $\langle\hat{D}\rangle = \tfrac{136}{77}$ and $h_{n} = 1 + \tfrac{68}{77}$). For the stored state $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + 2\hat\Omega(n)^{\dagger 2})\ket{0}$, which uses a word in $n$ itself, $\hat\Omega(n)\psi \ne 0$ and $h_{n} = \tfrac{1738}{199}$ lies above the floor, as (ii) requires.

\emph{(iv) What a selection rule has to fix.} In a source-built state, by (iii), $\lambda_{e} = 1 + \langle\hat{D}\rangle/2$ and the two heavier eigenvalues are $\lambda_{e} + g_{\pm}$, $g_{\pm}$ the eigenvalues of $G$ on $n^{\perp}$, with $g_{+} + g_{-} = \langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle + \tfrac32\langle\hat{D}\rangle$. Under the mass-squared reading of the skeleton theorem, $g_{\mu}/g_{\tau} = (m_{\mu}^{2} - m_{e}^{2})/(m_{\tau}^{2} - m_{e}^{2})$ and $(\lambda_{\mu} + \lambda_{\tau})/\lambda_{e} = (m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2}$. With the store's lepton masses (as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cumulants-at-fixed-second-moments-keep-the-floor}) the first is about $3.536 \times 10^{-3}$, and the second, about $1.2135 \times 10^{7}$, equals $2 + (\langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle + \tfrac32\langle\hat{D}\rangle)/(1 + \tfrac12\langle\hat{D}\rangle)$, so it fixes the ratio $\langle\hat{D}^{2}\rangle/\langle\hat{D}\rangle$ near $6.07 \times 10^{6}$ for large $\langle\hat{D}\rangle$; for a state of one degree $D$ it fixes $D$ between $6.066 \times 10^{6}$ and $6.069 \times 10^{6}$ (from $D(2D + 3)/(D + 2) = (m_{\mu}^{2} + m_{\tau}^{2})/m_{e}^{2} - 2$ over the $\tau$ mass interval; under a linear reading the same equation with $m/m_{e}$ in place of $m^{2}/m_{e}^{2}$ gives $D \approx 1841$ and $g_{\mu}/g_{\tau} \approx 0.0592$). These numbers are arithmetic on measured masses, computed outside the check; they are a dictionary for the state a rule would have to select, not a prediction. The Gaussian class of the skeleton is a special case: its pair-number distribution has mean $2x$ and variance $2x(1 + x)$, so (ii) gives the light eigenvalue $1 + x = \cosh^{2}r$ and $\mathrm{tr}\,H = 3 + 8x + 6x^{2}$, the theorem's $2(1 + x) + (1 + 6x + 6x^{2})$; for states with the skeleton's second moments the floor $1 + \langle\hat{N}\rangle/4$ is the floor $\cosh^{2}r$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cumulants-at-fixed-second-moments-keep-the-floor}, here reached on all of $\mathcal{S}$ without fixing the second moments. Remark on quasi-free states: a pure quasi-free state of zero mean is $\exp(\tfrac12 a^{\dagger}Ka^{\dagger})\ket{0}$ up to normalisation, fixed by its degree-two component; if it lies in $\mathcal{S}$, that component lies in $\mathrm{span}\{\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\ket{0}\}$, so the state is $\exp(\hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger})\ket{0}$ for some $v$, a polynomial in the single word $\hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger}$, and by (ii) its $G$ is annihilated on $v^{\perp}$ (since $\hat\Omega(y)$ differentiates along $y \perp v$ to zero), so its light pair is degenerate at the floor. On $\mathcal{S}$ every split of the light pair therefore needs a state outside the quasi-free class.
