synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-s.formal:
Let $a_{iA}$ be the six bosonic face modes, $\hat\Omega_{k}$ the face operators, $H(\psi)$ the mass form of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift} in an arbitrary state (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}), $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} = \sum_{k}\bar{c}_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$, and $N(U) = \overline{\det U}\,U$ the face action of the family unitary $U$, under which $H(\hat{U}\psi) = N H(\psi) N^{\dagger}$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-source-stabiliser}(i)). Let $v = \kappa(u' + \lambda e^{I_4\chi}f_{+})$, $\lambda > 0$ (numbers, including Fock amplitudes and the entries of family unitaries, and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_4$ commutes with the tower vectors, and the bar reverses $I_4$), be the coherent face vector of an antisymmetric pairing (Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}) and $\sigma = \sigma_{x,y} = (xP_{s} + yP_{d})\circ\overline{\phantom{v}}$, $|x| = |y| = 1$, any of the $S_{3}$-equivariant real structures of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(i), among them the four $C$-compatible ones ($x, y = \pm1$) and the Lorentzian quarter-turn structure $\sigma_{-1,1}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-turn}. Write $a = \lambda/\sqrt2$, so $a = 1$ at the Koide point $\lambda^{2} = 2$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Normal form.)} There is a face unitary $M = F R_{\delta} Q^{\dagger}$ ($Q = x^{1/2}P_{s} + y^{1/2}P_{d}$ for a choice of square roots, the slice map of $\sigma$, for $\sigma_{-1,1}$ the quarter-turn $Q = P_{d} - I_4 P_{s}$; $R_{\delta}$ a rotation about the democratic axis; $F$ the orthonormal frame $u, d_{1}, d_{2}$) with $M\sigma M^{-1}$ complex conjugation and
\[
Mv \;=\; e^{I_4\alpha}\sqrt3\,|\kappa|\,(1,\ a,\ I_4 a).
\]
with $e^{I_4\alpha} = \overline{x^{1/2}}\,\kappa/|\kappa|$: the normal form is that of the line $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\,v$, and its phase depends on $\sigma$ (and on the choice of square root) but not on the channel phase $\chi$, which the rotation $R_{\delta}$ absorbs together with the slice phase $\delta$ ($\delta = \chi - \pi/2$ for $\sigma_{-1,1}$, $\delta = \chi$ for $\sigma_{-1,-1}$). The phase matters for completions with fixed coefficients (in $1 + \hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger} + \hat\Omega(\sigma v)^{\dagger}$ the two words acquire the relative phase $e^{-2I_4\alpha}$) and not for the symmetry statements below. Consequently every completion built from $\hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\sigma v)^{\dagger}$ and $U(3)$-invariant words, or words defined in the normal frame, has a mass-form spectrum independent of $\chi$, in agreement with Proposition \claimref{synthesis.channel-phase-invisible-to-axially-covariant-completions}; $S_{3}$-invariant words that are not $U(3)$-invariant, written in the family frame, such as the cubic word of (iv), can see $\chi$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The residual stabiliser is $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$.)} In the frame of (i), with $c = (1, a, I_4 a) = c_{R} + I_4 c_{I}$, the unitaries commuting with conjugation and fixing $c$ are the real orthogonal matrices fixing $c_{R}$ and $c_{I}$, namely $\{1, R_{n}\}$ with $R_{n} = 1 - 2nn^{\mathsf T}/|n|^{2}$ the reflection in the plane of the source and $n = c_{R}\times c_{I} \propto (a, -1, 0)$; $R_{n} = N(I_4 R_{n})$ is in the face action, and at the Koide point it is the transposition of the two real axes. Its commutant has complex dimension $5$. Hence in every state invariant under $\hat{U}$, $U = I_4 R_{n}$, in particular every state built from $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ and $U(3)$-invariant words, $n$ is an exact eigenvector of $H$, and $H$ is otherwise an arbitrary Hermitian form on the plane $n^{\perp} = \mathrm{span}\{c, m\}$, $m \propto c_{R} - I_4(1 + 2/\lambda^{2})\,c_{I}$. Carried back to the family coordinates, $n$ has real slice coordinates proportional to $a - \sqrt2\cos(\delta + 2\pi k/3)$, orthogonal to the projected vector $p_{k} \propto 1 + \lambda\cos(\delta + 2\pi k/3)$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(iii); at the Koide point $n \propto 2u' - p$, the reflection of the Koide vector through the democratic axis, itself a Koide vector ($Q = \tfrac23$). The phase rotation $e^{I_4\phi}P_{c} + (1 - P_{c})$ fixes $c$ up to phase and does not commute with conjugation: the cut from the $SU(2)$ of the stored result to $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ is the real structure's. The symmetry fixes the eigenvector $n$ and not its place in the mass ordering, which is an extra input of the state (see (iii)).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The rest is the state's; computed, exact, at $a = 1$.)} Eleven states built from $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ and $\hat{V} = \sum_{k}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}$ are invariant under $\hat{U}$ and have $n$ as an exact eigenvector; the affine span of their mass forms is the whole five-dimensional commutant, so covariance imposes no further relation. The truncated single source $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + \tfrac12\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger 2})\ket{0}$ keeps the source as an eigenvector and the pair degenerate; the two-word states tilt the heavy eigenvector off the source. In the real family $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + \hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger} + \beta\,\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger})\ket{0}$, $\beta \in \R$, which is invariant under the antiunitary implementing $\sigma$, the pair is degenerate at $\beta = 0$ (one real source, $2c_{R}$) and split with $\beta$-dependent values otherwise ($h_{n} = \tfrac{145}{77}$ at $\beta = 1$, $\tfrac{505}{257}$ at $\beta = 2$, $\tfrac{55}{32}$ at $\beta = -\tfrac12$). A Gaussian frozen vacuum invariant under that antiunitary has a real source and a degenerate pair.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(A cubic family word forces nothing.)} The word $\hat\Omega_{1}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{2}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger}$ is invariant exactly under the monomial unitaries whose $N$ has unit product of phases, and $|v_{k}|^{2} = |\kappa|^{2}(1 + \lambda^{2} + 2\lambda\cos(\chi + 2\pi k/3))$ are three distinct numbers unless two of the cosines coincide ($\chi \in \tfrac{\pi}{3}\mathbb{Z}$, which the physical phase is not), so the only monomial unitary fixing $v$ is the identity: a completion built from the source and the cubic word has no residual symmetry and its mass form is unconstrained.
\end{enumerate}
So the two second structures the open problem names act through covariance in opposite and equally insufficient ways: the real structure forces one eigenvector and leaves the split, and the position of that eigenvector in the ordering, to the state; the cubic word leaves everything to the state. For these two structures a split with no second free number needs a rule selecting the non-Gaussian frozen vacuum, which the series does not supply; and the channel phase, which encodes the $207$ in the projection reading, is invisible to the real-structure completions. Observation, computed here on the eleven states and on $150$ random instances in exploration, and proved for the whole class in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.pair-singlet-mass-form-is-floor-plus-face-density}(iii): in every state built from the source, its conjugate and $\hat{V}$ the forced eigenvector $n$ is annihilated by $\hat\Omega(n)$ and sits at the floor $1 + \langle\hat{N}\rangle/4$, the least eigenvalue of $H$ (strictly the lowest when the pair is split), while the $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$-invariant word $(\hat\Omega(n)^{\dagger})^{2}$ puts it on top ($h_{n} = \tfrac{1738}{199}$ in the instance checked); so even which family the forced eigenvector is remains the state's.
synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-s.technical:
The stored stabiliser result says the electron and muon stay degenerate in any frozen vacuum that keeps the symmetry of its one source, and that a real structure on face space, already in the store, could break that symmetry. This result works out exactly what a real structure does. Any equivariant real structure, together with the coherent source of the families paper, can be rotated by a face unitary into a standard form: the structure becomes ordinary complex conjugation and the line of the source becomes that of the vector $(1, a, I_4 a)$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) with $a = \lambda/\sqrt2$, equal to $1$ at the Koide point, up to a phase that depends on the structure and not on the channel phase. The channel phase does not survive, so no completion built from the source, its conjugate and $U(3)$-invariant words can see the phase that encodes the muon-to-electron ratio.

In the standard form the symmetry left is a single reflection, the swap of the two real axes at the Koide point. A reflection forces one eigenvector of the mass form, the normal $n$ to the source's real plane, and nothing more: the remaining two-by-two block is free. Exact Fock computations confirm it, filling the whole five-parameter family, tilting the heavy direction off the source, and moving the split as the state's coefficients move; whether the forced eigenvector is the lightest family is also the state's, the lowest in every state built from the source, its conjugate and the invariant quartic word (it sits at the floor of the mass form there, as a later result proves for that whole class), and the top in an instance built with a word in the forced direction itself. Carried back to the family coordinates, $n$ is the Koide vector with its doublet reversed, the reflection of the square-root-mass vector through the democratic axis. A cubic family word, the other candidate, is invariant only under permutations with phases, none of which fixes a source whose three components have distinct moduli, so it constrains nothing. The conclusion is a reformulation for these two structures: the ratio $207$ cannot come from the real structure or the cubic family word acting through symmetry; it must come from the choice of non-Gaussian state, for which the series has no rule.
synthesis.real-structure-breaks-source-s.lay: The families paper leaves the electron and muon with equal masses, protected by a symmetry of the vacuum built from one preferred direction. One hoped-for cure was a notion of which directions in the family space count as real. This result shows what that notion can and cannot do. After a change of coordinates the preferred direction always looks the same, whichever version of reality is chosen and whatever the one free angle of the paper is, so that angle, which is where the muon-to-electron ratio would hide, is invisible. The symmetry that remains is a single mirror, and a mirror fixes only one thing: one definite direction in family space must be a mass eigenstate. Whether that state is the lightest, and how far apart the two light masses are, is not fixed at all; it depends on the detailed vacuum, and exact computations show every possibility is realised. A second candidate, a cubic combination of the three families, fixes even less. So for these two candidates the ratio of about 207 cannot be a consequence of symmetry; it would have to come from a rule choosing the vacuum, and no such rule is in the series.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i) The normal form.} By Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(i) the $S_{3}$-equivariant real structures are $\sigma_{x,y} = A\circ\overline{\phantom{v}}$ with $A = xP_{s} + yP_{d}$, $|x| = |y| = 1$, compatible with the bracket form exactly for $x, y = \pm1$. Choose a unitary $Q = x^{1/2}P_{s} + y^{1/2}P_{d}$ (any square roots); then on $P_{s}$ the product $Q^{\dagger}A\bar{Q}$ is $\overline{x^{1/2}}\,x\,\overline{x^{1/2}} = \bar{x}x = 1$, and likewise $\bar{y}y = 1$ on $P_{d}$, so $Q^{\dagger}A\bar{Q} = 1$; and for any unitary $M$ one has $M\sigma M^{-1} = (MAM^{\mathsf T})\circ\overline{\phantom{v}}$, since $\overline{M^{-1}w} = M^{\mathsf T}\bar{w}$. Hence $Q^{\dagger}\sigma Q = \overline{\phantom{v}}$, complex conjugation, and so does $M = FRQ^{\dagger}$ for every real orthogonal $F, R$, because $FRQ^{\dagger}A\bar{Q}R^{\mathsf T}F^{\mathsf T} = 1$. For $\sigma_{-1,1}$ the choice $Q = P_{d} - I_4 P_{s}$ is the quarter-turn of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-turn}; for $\sigma_{-1,-1}$, $Q = -I_4$; for $\sigma_{1,-1}$, $Q = P_{s} - I_4 P_{d}$. Now $Q^{\dagger}v = s_{0}(u' + w'f_{+})$ with $s_{0} = \bar{x}^{1/2}\kappa$ and $w' = \lambda e^{I_4\delta}$, $\delta = \chi + \arg(\bar{y}^{1/2}x^{1/2})$: for $\kappa = -I_4|\kappa|$ and $\sigma_{-1,1}$ this is $\delta = \chi - \pi/2$, the slice phase of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(iii), and for $\sigma_{-1,-1}$ it is $\delta = \chi$. Up to the overall phase $s_{0}/|\kappa|$ the vector is $u' + \lambda e^{I_4\delta}f_{+}$, whose real and imaginary parts in family coordinates are $1 + \lambda\cos\delta_{k}$ and $\lambda\sin\delta_{k}$, $\delta_{k} = \delta + 2\pi k/3$ (Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form} for $f_{+}$ and the Fourier lines). In the orthonormal frame $u = u'/\sqrt3$, $d_{1} = (2,-1,-1)/\sqrt6$, $d_{2} = (0,1,-1)/\sqrt2$ the doublet part of $e^{I_4\delta}f_{+}$ is $\sqrt{3/2}\,(d_{1}(\delta) + I_4\,d_{2}(\delta))$ with $d_{1}(\delta) = \cos\delta\,d_{1} - \sin\delta\,d_{2}$ and $d_{2}(\delta) = \sin\delta\,d_{1} + \cos\delta\,d_{2}$, the frame rotated by $\delta$ about $u$: the vector $(1, I_4)$ of the doublet plane is an eigenvector of every rotation of that plane. The rotation $R_{\delta}$ about the democratic axis by $-\delta$ (real orthogonal, commuting with $P_{s}$, $P_{d}$ and conjugation) carries it to $\sqrt{3/2}\,(d_{1} + I_4 d_{2})$, and the frame map $F$ (rows $u, d_{1}, d_{2}$) then gives
\[
M v \;=\; e^{I_4\alpha}\,|\kappa|\bigl(\sqrt3,\ \lambda\sqrt{3/2},\ I_4\lambda\sqrt{3/2}\bigr) \;=\; e^{I_4\alpha}\sqrt3\,|\kappa|\,(1, a, I_4 a), \qquad a = \lambda/\sqrt2 .
\]
Here $e^{I_4\alpha} = s_{0}/|\kappa| = \overline{x^{1/2}}\,\kappa/|\kappa|$ (for the quarter-turn $Q = P_{d} - I_4 P_{s}$ and $\kappa = -I_4|\kappa|$ it is $1$): the normal form is that of the line $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\,v$; its phase depends on $\sigma$ through $x$ and on the choice of square root, not on $\chi$, and it enters completions with fixed coefficients, since $1 + \hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger} + \hat\Omega(\sigma v)^{\dagger}$ is carried to $1 + e^{-I_4\alpha}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + e^{I_4\alpha}\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ with $c = \sqrt3|\kappa|(1, a, I_4 a)$ (as $\hat\Omega(e^{I_4\alpha}c)^{\dagger} = e^{-I_4\alpha}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$ and $M\sigma v = \overline{Mv}$), a relative phase $e^{-2I_4\alpha}$ between the two words; the symmetry statements of (ii) are insensitive to it. Neither $\sigma$ nor $\chi$ is left in the line. The check verifies, in exact arithmetic in $\Q(\sqrt2,\sqrt3)(I_4)$, for $\sigma_{-1,1}$ at $(a, \cos\chi) = (1, \tfrac35), (\tfrac23, \tfrac5{13}), (1, \tfrac5{13})$, for $\sigma_{-1,-1}$ and for $\sigma_{1,-1}$ at $(1, \tfrac35)$: $Q^{\dagger}A\bar{Q} = 1$, $M$ unitary, $MAM^{\mathsf T} = 1$, $|w'| = \lambda$, and $Mv = e^{I_4\alpha}\sqrt3(1, a, I_4 a)$ with $|e^{I_4\alpha}| = 1$. The consequence for completions: a state built from $\hat\Omega(v)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\sigma v)^{\dagger}$ and $U(3)$-invariant words is carried by the Fock unitary $\hat{U}$ with $N(U) = M$ (every unitary is some $N(U)$, as $N(e^{I_4\theta}1) = e^{-2I_4\theta}$ and $N(U) = U$ on $SU(3)$) to the same construction on $(Mv, \overline{\phantom{v}})$, by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-source-stabiliser}(i), the invariant words being unchanged; its mass form is $MHM^{\dagger}$, with the same spectrum; and the construction in the frame does not contain $\chi$. The same holds for words defined in the normal frame. It does not hold for words fixed in the family frame that are only $S_{3}$-invariant, such as the cubic word of (iv): $M$ depends on $\chi$ through $R_{\delta}$, so such a word is carried to a $\chi$-dependent word in the frame, and the spectrum can depend on $\chi$, which is the stored statement that only family-basis structure can see the channel phase. This is the mechanism of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.channel-phase-invisible-to-axially-covariant-completions}: the rotation about the democratic axis that shifts $\chi$ commutes with every equivariant real structure.

\emph{(ii) The residual stabiliser.} In the frame, $c = (1, a, I_4 a) = c_{R} + I_4 c_{I}$ with $c_{R} = (1, a, 0)$, $c_{I} = (0, 0, a)$, independent for $a > 0$. A unitary $N$ commuting with conjugation is real, hence real orthogonal; $Nc = c$ then gives $Nc_{R} = c_{R}$ and $Nc_{I} = c_{I}$, so $N - 1$ vanishes on the plane $\mathrm{span}\{c_{R}, c_{I}\}$ and $N = 1 + yn^{\mathsf T}$ for some $y$, with $n = c_{R}\times c_{I} = (a^{2}, -a, 0) \propto (a, -1, 0)$ the normal (the check computes the kernel $\{X : Xc_{R} = Xc_{I} = 0\}$ exactly and finds dimension $3$). Orthogonality, $N^{\mathsf T}N = 1$, reads $ny^{\mathsf T} + yn^{\mathsf T} + |y|^{2}nn^{\mathsf T} = 0$; contracting with a vector orthogonal to $n$ forces $y \parallel n$, $y = tn$, and then $2t + t^{2}|n|^{2} = 0$: $t = 0$ or $t = -2/|n|^{2}$. So the stabiliser is $\{1, R_{n}\}$, $R_{n}$ the reflection in the source's real plane; it is in the face action since $N(I_4 R_{n}) = \overline{\det(I_4 R_{n})}\,I_4 R_{n} = \overline{I_4^{3}\det R_{n}}\,I_4 R_{n} = \overline{(-I_4)(-1)}\,I_4 R_{n} = \overline{I_4}\,I_4 R_{n}$, that is $\det(I_4 R_{n}) = I_4^{3}\det R_{n} = I_4$ and $N = (-I_4)(I_4)R_{n} = R_{n}$. At $a = 1$, $n = (1, -1, 0)$ and $R_{n}$ is the transposition of the first two axes. Its commutant in $M_{3}(\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\})$ is $\{X : X_{11} = X_{22}, X_{12} = X_{21}, X_{13} = X_{23}, X_{31} = X_{32}\}$, of complex dimension $5$ (the check solves $XR_{n} = R_{n}X$ over $\Q$ as a real linear system). If $\hat{U}\psi = \psi$ for $U = I_4 R_{n}$, then $H = R_{n}HR_{n}$ by covariance, so $Hn = h_{n}n$ and $H$ preserves $n^{\perp}$, where it is an arbitrary Hermitian form; states built from $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ and $U(3)$-invariant words are invariant because $R_{n}c = c$, $R_{n}\bar{c} = \overline{R_{n}c} = \bar{c}$ ($R_{n}$ real) and $\hat{U}\ket{0} = \ket{0}$, by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-source-stabiliser}(i). The plane $n^{\perp}$ is $\{\alpha c_{R} + \beta c_{I} : \alpha, \beta \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}\} \ni c$, and the Hermitian complement of $c$ in it is $m = c_{R} - I_4(|c_{R}|^{2}/|c_{I}|^{2})c_{I} = c_{R} - I_4(1 + 2/\lambda^{2})c_{I}$, since $|c_{R}|^{2} = 1 + a^{2}$ and $|c_{I}|^{2} = a^{2}$. The phase rotation $e^{I_4\phi}P_{c} + (1 - P_{c})$ fixes $c$ up to phase, lies in the $U(2)$ of the stored stabiliser result, and is not real for $\phi \notin \pi\mathbb{Z}$: the check exhibits it at $e^{I_4\phi} = \tfrac35 + \tfrac45 I_4$.

Carried back: $n_{\mathrm{orig}} = M^{\dagger}n$ has slice coordinates $Q^{\dagger}n_{\mathrm{orig}} = R_{\delta}^{\mathsf T}F^{\mathsf T}(a, -1, 0)^{\mathsf T} = au - d_{1}(\delta)$, real, with family coordinates $a/\sqrt3 - \sqrt{2/3}\cos\delta_{k} \propto a - \sqrt2\cos\delta_{k}$, because $(d_{1}(\delta))_{k} = \sqrt{2/3}\cos(\delta + 2\pi k/3)$. The projected vector of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.coherent-face-vector-real-slices}(iii) has coordinates $p_{k} = |\kappa|(1 + \lambda\cos\delta_{k})$, and $\sum_{k}(a - \sqrt2\cos\delta_{k})(1 + \lambda\cos\delta_{k}) = 3a - \sqrt2\lambda\cdot\tfrac32 = 0$ for $a = \lambda/\sqrt2$, using $\sum_{k}\cos\delta_{k} = 0$ and $\sum_{k}\cos^{2}\delta_{k} = \tfrac32$. At $a = 1$, $1 - \sqrt2\cos\delta_{k} = 2 - p_{k}/|\kappa|$, so $n \propto 2u' - p$, the reflection of $p$ through the democratic axis ($2(p\cdot u)u - p$ with $p\cdot u = \sqrt3|\kappa|$), and $\sum_{k}n_{k}^{2} = 3 + 2\cdot\tfrac32 = 6 = \tfrac23(\sum_{k}n_{k})^{2}$: a Koide vector. The check verifies the reality of the slice coordinates, the proportionality to $a - \sqrt2\cos\delta_{k}$ (with $\cos\delta_{k}$ read off $w'f_{+}$ exactly), both orthogonalities and, at $a = 1$, the reflection identity and $Q = \tfrac23$, in all five cases of (i).

\emph{(iii) The free block; computed.} The check works in the six-mode Fock space of the stored stabiliser check, with the face operators $\hat\Omega_{k} = \tfrac12\sum\epsilon_{kij}\epsilon_{AB}a_{iA}a_{jB}$ of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift} and the mass form in an arbitrary state of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.face-mass-form-unit-plus-gram}, exact complex-rational amplitudes, at $a = 1$. The eleven states are the truncated single source $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + \tfrac12\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger 2})\ket{0}$; six two-word states with coefficients in $\Q(I_4)$ using $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$ and $\hat{V}$ (listed in the check); and the real family at $\beta = 0, 1, 2, -\tfrac12$. For each: $\hat{U}\psi = \psi$ with $U = I_4 P_{12}$ (the Fock map of the stored check), $H$ in the commutant of $P_{12}$, and $Hn = h_{n}n$ with $n = (1, -1, 0)$, $h_{n} = H_{11} - H_{12}$. In the basis $(1,1,0)/\sqrt2$, $e_{3}$ of $n^{\perp}$ the block is $B = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} H_{11} + H_{12} & \sqrt2 H_{13}\\ \sqrt2\bar{H}_{13} & H_{33}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, and $h_{n}$ lies below both eigenvalues of $B$ exactly when $\det(B - h_{n}) > 0$ and $\mathrm{tr}\,B - 2h_{n} > 0$, above both when $\det(B - h_{n}) > 0$ and $\mathrm{tr}\,B - 2h_{n} < 0$. The five real coordinates $(H_{11}, H_{12}, \mathrm{Re}\,H_{13}, \mathrm{Im}\,H_{13}, H_{33})$ of the eleven forms have differences of rank $5$: the affine span is the whole commutant. The truncated single source has $h_{n} = \tfrac{32}{17}$, discriminant zero and $Hc \parallel c$ (the skeleton's alignment); the state $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + \tfrac23\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger})\ket{0}$ has $h_{n} = \tfrac{190}{101}$, three distinct eigenvalues and $Hc \not\parallel c$. In the real family, $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + \hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(c + \bar{c})^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(2c_{R})^{\dagger}$ and $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger} = \sum_{kl}\mathrm{Re}(\bar{c}_{k}c_{l})\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}^{\dagger}$ (the $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ commute), so for real $\beta$ the amplitudes are real: the state is invariant under the antiunitary $\hat{J}$ that conjugates Fock amplitudes, which implements $\sigma$ in the frame ($\hat{J}\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}\hat{J} = \hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$, the $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ being real). At $\beta = 0$ it is a single real source, degenerate by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-source-stabiliser}(iv); at $\beta = 1, 2, -\tfrac12$ it is split, with $h_{n} = \tfrac{145}{77}$ ($B$: $\tfrac{521}{77}$, $0$, $\tfrac{229}{77}$), $\tfrac{505}{257}$ and $\tfrac{55}{32}$. A Gaussian state $\exp(\hat\Omega(x)^{\dagger})\ket{0}$ is $\hat{J}$-invariant exactly when $\hat\Omega(x)^{\dagger} = \hat\Omega(\bar{x})^{\dagger}$, that is $x$ real, and real sources leave the pair degenerate; the Gaussian class (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}) gains nothing from reality. In all eight split instances $\det(B - h_{n}) > 0$ and $\mathrm{tr}\,B - 2h_{n} > 0$: $n$ is the lowest eigenvector. The $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$-invariant word $(\hat\Omega(n)^{\dagger})^{2}$ (invariant since $\hat\Omega(R_{n}n)^{\dagger} = -\hat\Omega(n)^{\dagger}$) reverses this: $(1 + \hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger} + 2\hat\Omega(n)^{\dagger 2})\ket{0}$ has $h_{n} = \tfrac{1738}{199}$ above both eigenvalues of $B$. In exploration (work folder, not part of the check) $150$ random states with coefficients in $\Q(I_4)$ and words of length up to four in $\hat\Omega(c)^{\dagger}$, $\hat\Omega(\bar{c})^{\dagger}$, $\hat{V}$ gave $85$ split instances, all with $n$ lowest; no proof is offered, and the statement is recorded as an observation.

\emph{(iv) The cubic family word.} Under $\hat{U}$, $\hat\Omega(e_{k})^{\dagger} \mapsto \hat\Omega(Ne_{k})^{\dagger}$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.light-pair-split-needs-broken-source-stabiliser}(i)), so the word $\hat{W} = \hat\Omega_{1}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{2}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{3}^{\dagger}$ maps to $\prod_{k}\hat\Omega(Ne_{k})^{\dagger}$, which equals $\hat{W}$ exactly when $\{Ne_{k}\}$ is $\{d_{k}e_{\pi(k)}\}$ with $\prod_{k}\bar{d}_{k} = 1$ (the $\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}$ commute, so any permutation $\pi$ is allowed and $\hat\Omega(de)^{\dagger} = \bar{d}\hat\Omega(e)^{\dagger}$): the monomial group with unit product of phases. The check verifies invariance under the Fock maps of $N = \mathrm{diag}(I_4, -I_4, 1)$ and of a $3$-cycle with phases $(I_4, 1, -I_4)$, and non-invariance under a real rotation of the first two families. A monomial $N$ with $Nv = v$ needs $d_{k}v_{\pi^{-1}(k)} = v_{k}$, so $|v_{k}| = |v_{\pi^{-1}(k)}|$ for all $k$; by Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}, $v_{k} = \kappa(1 + \lambda e^{I_4\chi}\zeta^{k})$ and $|v_{k}|^{2} = |\kappa|^{2}(1 + \lambda^{2} + 2\lambda\cos(\chi + 2\pi k/3))$, three distinct numbers unless $\cos\chi_{j} = \cos\chi_{k}$ for some $j \ne k$, which happens exactly for $\chi \in \tfrac{\pi}{3}\mathbb{Z}$; then $\pi = 1$ and $d_{k} = 1$. The check computes the three moduli exactly at $\lambda = \sqrt2$ for $\cos\chi = \tfrac35$ and $\tfrac5{13}$ (distinct; only the identity permutation preserves them) and at $\chi = 2\pi/3$ (two coincide). The physical phase of the projection reading, $\delta = 0.222$, $\chi = \delta + \pi/2 \approx 1.79$, is not in $\tfrac{\pi}{3}\mathbb{Z}$ (nearest members $1.05$ and $2.09$). So a completion built from the source and the cubic word is covariant under nothing, and its mass form is unconstrained by symmetry; by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.channel-phase-invisible-to-axially-covariant-completions} it is also the only kind that can see $\chi$ at all.

\emph{Conclusion.} The stored result required a second face-space structure breaking the source's stabiliser. The two candidates it named do break it, to $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ and to the trivial group, and in both cases what covariance then fixes is at most one eigenvector; the split is a function of the state's coefficients, which the series does not fix, and the real structure cannot even see the channel phase. Hence no construction of this kind produces $m_{\mu}/m_{e}$ with no second free number, and the open problem's remaining content is a rule selecting the non-Gaussian frozen vacuum.

synthesis.slot-covariance-forces-gram-sq.formal:
Let $Z^{1}, Z^{2}, Z^{3} \in \CS$ be a three-spinor composite with the conventions of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.many-twistor-join}: $B^{il}_{\Lambda} = \ip{I_{\Lambda}}{Z^{i} \wedge Z^{l}}$ and the Gram matrix $h$. Call $\beta_{k} := B^{ij}_{\Lambda}$, $(i, j)$ the cyclic successors of $k$, the face vector, and let the slot mixing $Z^{i} \mapsto \sum_{j} Z^{j}U_{ji}$, $U \in U(3)$, be the internal group of the three-spinor system (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder}). A face form is a Hermitian matrix $M(Z)$ on face space; it is covariant if $M(Z \cdot U) = \overline{R_{U}}\,M(Z)\,R_{U}^{\mathsf T}$ for all $U$, with $R_{U}$ as in (i).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The cofactor law.)} $\beta \mapsto R_{U}\beta$ with $R_{U} = \det(U)\,U^{-1}$, and $h \mapsto U^{\dagger}hU$; $U \mapsto R_{U}$ maps $U(3)$ onto $U(3)$, and on permutations it is the sign-twisted action $\Omega \mapsto \pm P\Omega$ of Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}(1).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The Gram square, forced.)} The covariant face forms $M_{kl} = \sum_{m,n} A_{kl}^{mn}\,\bar\beta_{m}\beta_{n}$ with constant coefficients are exactly $a\,\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T} + b\,|\beta|^{2}\,\mathbb{1}$. Exactly one of them has the face-wise diagonal $M_{kk} = 2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$, each face's own two-spinor bracket term:
\[
M \;=\; 2\,\bar\beta\,\beta^{\mathsf T},
\]
the Gram square of the face map $Z \mapsto \beta(Z)$. Its trace is the bracket part of the three-spinor join, $\tr M = 2\sum_{i<l}|B^{il}_{\Lambda}|^{2} = m^{2} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}C_{3}$, and in every configuration it is positive semidefinite of rank at most one, with spectrum $(2|\beta|^{2}, 0, 0)$ and eigenvector $\bar\beta$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The permutations alone do not force it.)} The permutation-covariant face forms with constant coefficients and face-wise diagonal $M_{kk} = 2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$, covariant under the sign-twisted permutations only, form a nine-dimensional complex affine space (the Gram square plus the nine-dimensional space of covariant zero-diagonal tensors). It contains the face-wise form $2\operatorname{diag}(|\beta_{k}|^{2})$, positive semidefinite, of rank three for generic $\beta$ and with three degenerate families at the democratic direction, and the forms $2\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T} + c\,(\J - \mathbb{1})|\beta|^{2}$, indefinite for every real $c \neq 0$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The cosmological term.)} The faces' full two-spinor joins sum to the composite's,
\[
\sum_{k}\Bigl(2|\beta_{k}|^{2} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,C(h_{k})\Bigr) \;=\; m^{2} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}\sum_{i} h_{ii}^{2},
\]
with $h_{k}$ the $2 \times 2$ block of face $k$, and for $\Lambda \neq 0$ no covariant face form in the span of $\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}$, $|\beta|^{2}\mathbb{1}$, $\bar h^{2}$, $(\tr h)\bar h$, $\tr(h^{2})\mathbb{1}$, $(\tr h)^{2}\mathbb{1}$ has these joins as its diagonal.
\end{enumerate}
So, for a family form sesquilinear in the face vector with constant coefficients and with the face-wise diagonal, covariance of the mass law under the slot $U(3)$, which is Premise \claimref{families.slot-covariance-of-mass-law}, makes it the Gram square of the face vector, exactly at $\Lambda = 0$ and for the bracket part at any $\Lambda$, and classically one family is massive in every configuration.
synthesis.slot-covariance-forces-gram-sq.technical:
In a three-spinor composite, the frozen point's pairing with the three two-spinor faces gives a face vector $\beta$ whose components are the faces' mass brackets. Under the slot mixing $U(3)$ of the internal-symmetry ladder, $\beta$ transforms by the cofactor law $\beta \mapsto \det(U)U^{-1}\beta$, which on permutations is the families paper's sign-twisted action. By Schur's lemma the covariant Hermitian forms on face space that are sesquilinear in $\beta$ form a two-parameter family, $a\,\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T} + b\,|\beta|^{2}\mathbb{1}$, and requiring each diagonal entry to be that face's own two-spinor mass term $2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$ fixes $a = 2$, $b = 0$: the family form is the Gram square $2\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}$, whose trace is the bracket part of the three-spinor join and which has rank one in every configuration.

The content of the Gram-square property comes from the sesquilinear-in-$\beta$ ansatz: every positive semidefinite form is a Gram matrix of some map, and what is derived here is that it is the rank-one square of the face map itself (the point raised in the light-cone result filed alongside, synthesis.light-cone-koide-is-quarter-turn). The permutations alone do not force this: the permutation-covariant forms with the face-wise diagonal form a nine-dimensional affine space, including the purely face-wise form $2\operatorname{diag}(|\beta_{k}|^{2})$, positive and with three equal families at the democratic point, so it is the continuous slot symmetry, equivalently the internal $U(2)$ of every pair of slots, that selects the Gram square. That symmetry of the mass law is assumed, as the premise of slot covariance (a flavour symmetry of the law broken by the state), and the Gram square holds under it. At $\Lambda \neq 0$ the faces' Casimir terms add up to the composite's plus $(\Lambda/12)\sum_{i}h_{ii}^{2}$, which is not $U(3)$ invariant, and no covariant form built from the join's ingredients has the faces' full joins on its diagonal.
synthesis.slot-covariance-forces-gram-sq.lay: The families paper explains why one generation of matter is much heavier than the other two by assuming that the table of family masses has a special "square" form, which automatically leaves room for only one heavy family. This result derives that form instead of assuming it. In a three-part composite, each pair of parts carries a mass, and the parts can be mixed among themselves by a continuous symmetry. If the rule that assigns masses is built directly from the pairs' masses and respects that symmetry, which is assumed here as a premise, there are only two candidate mass tables, and requiring each pair's own mass to appear on the diagonal leaves exactly the square form. Swapping the parts around, without continuous mixing, would not be enough: it also allows a table in which the three families are equally heavy. A small correction from the cosmological constant does not fit the symmetric rule.

proofs.main:
(i) By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.many-twistor-join}(3), $B_{\Lambda} \mapsto U^{\mathsf T}B_{\Lambda}U$ and $h \mapsto U^{\dagger}hU$. Write the antisymmetric $B_{\Lambda}$ as $B_{ij} = \varepsilon_{ijk}\beta_{k}$. Then $(U^{\mathsf T}BU)_{ij} = \sum_{p,q}U_{pi}U_{qj}\varepsilon_{pqm}\beta_{m}$, and the cofactor identity $\sum_{p,q}\varepsilon_{pqm}U_{pi}U_{qj} = \det(U)\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}(U^{-1})_{km}$ gives $\beta \mapsto \det(U)U^{-1}\beta$. The map $U \mapsto \det(U)U^{-1}$ is onto $U(3)$: for $V \in U(3)$ pick $\mu$ with $\mu^{2} = \det V$ and put $U = \mu V^{-1}$, so that $\det U = \mu^{3}/\det V = \mu$ and $\det(U)U^{-1} = V$. For a permutation matrix $P$, $\det(P)P^{-1} = \operatorname{sgn}(P)P^{\mathsf T}$, the sign twist of Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}(1). That the slot mixings form exactly $U(3)$ is Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder}.

(ii) Since $R_{U}$ runs over all of $U(3)$ by (i), covariance says that the tensor $A$ is invariant under $U(3)$ acting on $\bar V \otimes V \otimes V \otimes \bar V$ (indices $k$, $l$ of the form, $m$ and $n$ of $\bar\beta_{m}\beta_{n}$), with $V = \C^{3}$ irreducible. The invariant tensors pair each $V$ index with a $\bar V$ index: $\delta_{km}\delta_{ln}$ and $\delta_{kl}\delta_{mn}$, so $M = a\,\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T} + b\,|\beta|^{2}\mathbb{1}$, and Hermiticity makes $a$, $b$ real. The check confirms the count independently: the infinitesimal covariance conditions for the nine generators of $\uu(3)$, solved in exact Gaussian-rational arithmetic, have a two-dimensional solution space. The diagonal is $M_{kk} = a|\beta_{k}|^{2} + b|\beta|^{2}$; the face-wise condition $M_{kk} = 2|\beta_{k}|^{2}$ for all configurations, at a configuration with $\beta_{k} = 0 \neq \beta_{l}$, gives $b = 0$, and then $a = 2$ (equivalently, the covariance conditions together with a zero diagonal have only the zero solution). The face-wise diagonal is the bracket term of the two-spinor join of face $k$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.many-twistor-join}(2) at $N = 2$, whose $B^{ij}_{\Lambda}$ is $\beta_{k}$. The trace is $2|\beta|^{2} = 2\sum_{i<l}|B^{il}_{\Lambda}|^{2}$, the bracket part of the same Theorem at $N = 3$. For any $c \in \C^{3}$, $\bar c^{\mathsf T}M c = 2|\beta^{\mathsf T}c|^{2} \ge 0$, every $2 \times 2$ minor of $\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}$ vanishes, and $M\bar\beta = 2|\beta|^{2}\bar\beta$.

(iii) The sign-twisted permutations are generated by $-P_{(12)}$ and the cyclic $P_{(123)}$; the invariance conditions for these two, solved exactly, leave a fourteen-dimensional space of tensors, of which the zero-diagonal ones form a nine-dimensional subspace, so the covariant forms with the face-wise diagonal are the Gram square plus that subspace, a nine-dimensional affine space. The tensor of $\operatorname{diag}(|\beta_{k}|^{2})$ is invariant under them (the permutations permute the $|\beta_{k}|^{2}$ and the sign squares away) and fails the $\uu(3)$ conditions; likewise $(\J - \mathbb{1})|\beta|^{2}$, since $P\J P^{\mathsf T} = \J$. At $\beta = (1, 0, 0)$, $2\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T} + c(\J - \mathbb{1})$ has the principal minor $\begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & c \\ c & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}$ of determinant $-c^{2} < 0$, so it is indefinite for $c \neq 0$. At the democratic direction $\beta \propto (1,1,1)$ the face-wise form is a multiple of the identity.

(iv) For a $2 \times 2$ block, $C(h_{k}) = \tfrac12\tr h_{k}^{2} - \tfrac14(\tr h_{k})^{2} = \tfrac14(h_{ii} - h_{jj})^{2} + |h_{ij}|^{2}$, and summing over the three faces against $C_{3} = \tfrac12\tr(h^{2}) - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.many-twistor-join}(2) gives $\sum_{k}C(h_{k}) - C_{3} = \tfrac14\sum_{i}h_{ii}^{2}$; with the bracket parts this is the displayed sum. Each of the six listed forms is covariant: $\bar h \mapsto U^{\mathsf T}\bar h\bar U = \overline{R_{U}}\,\bar h\,R_{U}^{\mathsf T}$, the determinant phases cancelling. Suppose $a\bar\beta\beta^{\mathsf T} + b|\beta|^{2}\mathbb{1} + \alpha_{1}\bar h^{2} + \alpha_{2}(\tr h)\bar h + \alpha_{3}\tr(h^{2})\mathbb{1} + \alpha_{4}(\tr h)^{2}\mathbb{1}$ had diagonal $2|\beta_{k}|^{2} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}C(h_{k})$. All diagonal entries are real, so this is a real linear system for $(a, b, \alpha_{1}, \ldots, \alpha_{4})$, one equation per face and configuration. On the twelve configurations of the check (four composites, three nonzero values of $\Lambda$) its coefficient matrix has rank six and its augmented matrix rank seven, so it has no solution. At $\Lambda = 0$ the same system has rank six and is solved by $a = 2$ and all other coefficients zero, consistent with (ii). By hand: comparing the coefficients of $h_{ii}h_{jj}$, $h_{kk}^{2}$, $h_{ii}^{2}$, $h_{kk}h_{ii}$ and $|h_{ki}|^{2}$ in the $k$-th diagonal entry forces $\alpha_{4} = -\tfrac14$, $\alpha_{3} = \tfrac12$, $\alpha_{2} = \tfrac12$, $\alpha_{1} = -\tfrac34$ and then $\alpha_{1} + 2\alpha_{3} = 0$, which fails.

The closing sentence collects (ii) and (iv); the covariance it applies to the mass law is Premise \claimref{families.slot-covariance-of-mass-law}. Two remarks, not part of the proof. First, the internal $U(2)$ of each pair of slots (the two-spinor case of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder}, under which that face's bracket picks up $\det$) is a subgroup of the slot $U(3)$, and the Lie algebras of the three pairwise $U(2)$ together span $\uu(3)$, so covariance under each pair's $U(2)$ is the same hypothesis as covariance under $U(3)$. Second, the same argument applies verbatim to the face operators $\hat\Omega_{k}$ of the families paper's six-mode face algebra under the passive mixing $a_{iA} \mapsto \sum_{j}U_{ji}a_{jA}$, since they are built from the same antisymmetric $\varepsilon$-contraction: the unique covariant normal-ordered face form with face-wise diagonal $\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{k}\rangle$ is $\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle$, the normal-ordered part of the mass form of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}; this operator transcription is argued, not separately machine-checked.

synthesis.slot-module-makes-the-faces-se.formal:
Let $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ be a composite's state space of the form assumed by Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}, in the setting of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}, with slot number $n$, pair number $k$ and $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$; the statements below hold for state spaces satisfying the premise's clauses named in them, and are conditional on the premise where they are applied to the series' composites.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Two slots per composite; clause (G) restated.)} If $F$ is graded as in clause (a), the one-slot space $F_{1}$ is a polynomial representation of the slot mixing $U(2)$ on which $\mu I_{2}$ acts as $\mu$; the polynomial irreducible representations of degree one are the doublet alone, so $F_{1}$ is a sum of doublets, of even dimension. If moreover $F$ is generated as in (G), $F_{1}$ is the image of $\C^{2} \otimes F_{0}$ with $\dim F_{0} = 1$, so $F_{1} \cong \C^{2}$ (or $F_{1} = 0$), as the premise itself states. No action of $U(2)$ makes a three-dimensional slot space the one-slot space of a composite.
\item \emph{(The shared space is no slot module, even for one face.)} Let $S = \C^{3}$ be the slot space of the three-spinor composite, $W = \C^{3}$, and read $\Lambda^{\bullet}(S \oplus W)$ with the gauge group $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ of one face $S_{F}$ ($U(2)$ on $S_{F}$, trivial on the remaining slot $s_{o}$). If the slot number counts all three slots, the centre of $U(2)$ acts trivially on $s_{o}$, of slot number one, against (a). If it counts the face's slots only, $F_{0} = \mathrm{span}\{1, s_{o}\}$ has dimension two, against (G): every weight occurs exactly twice, $\Lambda^{\bullet}(S \oplus W) \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}(S_{F} \oplus W) \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C s_{o})$, which is the premise's own refutation signature (two copies of each species), and the half of even mode number carries the face's particle half once and its antiparticle half once, so it is vectorlike. This complements Theorem \claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}(3), which already gives that, with shared slots, the faces are three generations only as separate composites: the shared space fails the premise even before a second face is considered, so if each generation satisfies the premise under one gauge group, the faces of Theorem \claimref{families.three-identical-families-mixing-shared-slots} are three separate composites $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W_{F})$, each with its own two slots and its own pair system.
\item \emph{(The number is free; standard.)} For every $n \ge 1$, if one composite satisfies the premise then $n$ separate copies satisfy every clause of it, each for itself, and their particle halves, $16n$ states, satisfy the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} and the colour cubic condition, each sum being $n$ times its value $0$ for one copy; the number of weak doublets is $4n$, even, as Witten's global anomaly requires (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-witten-global-su2-anomaly}). So the number of generations is independent of the slot-module premise and of anomaly freedom.
\item \emph{(Asymptotic freedom bounds it, if required; standard.)} Under the Krein premise (\claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}), with the coefficients of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}, one copy's Dynkin sums are $2$ for $\su(2)$ and $2$ for $\su(3)$, so $b_{3} = -11 + \tfrac43 n$ and $b_{2} = -\tfrac{22}{3} + \tfrac43 n + \tfrac{n_{h}}{6}$: colour is asymptotically free exactly for $n \le 8$, and weak isospin exactly for $n \le 5$ when $n_{h} = 1$ or $2$ (the stored condition $8n_{g} + n_{h} < 44$ at these $n_{h}$). So if both non-abelian factors are to be asymptotically free, $1 \le n \le 5$; nothing in the store requires the weak factor to be.
\item \emph{(The face count; argued reading.)} Every bivector of a three-dimensional slot space is a blade, so the face planes are exactly the lines of $\Lambda^{2}S$, of dimension $3$, and $(Xa) \wedge (Xb)$ is $\det(X)X^{-\mathsf T}$ applied to $a \wedge b$ through the dual: $\Lambda^{2}S \cong S^{*} \otimes \det$ as a $GL(S)$-module, the dual triplet of the slot space twisted by the determinant; $\binom{N}{2} = N$ only for $N = 3$. \emph{Reading (argued, under a further hypothesis):} if the generation labels are taken to be the face space of the maximal composite, with the slot $\su(3)$ of the maximal hierarchy acting on them as a family symmetry, which neither the premise nor (2) implies (separate composites need no labels from the maximal composite), then the number of generations is $\dim\Lambda^{2}\C^{3} = 3$. This rests on that hypothesis and on the three-spinor bound, imported at observation level (Fact \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}); the count three is not derived.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.slot-module-makes-the-faces-se.technical: The slot-module hypothesis says a composite's slot states are built from one vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators. Clause (1) restates clause (G) in representation-theoretic form: clause (a) makes the one-slot space a sum of doublets, and (G) makes it exactly one, so every composite has two slots and the three-spinor composite's three slots cannot be one composite's slot space. Clause (2) complements the stored theorem that, with shared slots, the faces are three generations under one gauge group only as separate composites (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}(3)). Viewed with the gauge group of a single face, the shared space already fails the premise. Either it has a slot the centre does not count, or it has two slot vacua, which doubles every species, the premise's own refutation signature. Its chirality half is one generation together with its conjugate, a vectorlike pair. The number of separate composites is fixed neither by the premise nor by anomaly cancellation, which holds copy by copy for any number (standard per-generation cancellation). If both non-abelian factors are to be asymptotically free, the stored one-loop condition allows one to five (standard). On the data side, the stored count of light neutrino species from the $Z$ resonance (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}) bounds light neutrinos, not generations. Three appears only in a reading: the face space of three slots has dimension three and is the dual triplet of the slot space twisted by the determinant. Taking it as the generation label space, with the slot $\su(3)$ acting on the labels, is a further family-symmetry hypothesis, and the three-spinor bound that supplies three slots is imported at observation level.
synthesis.slot-module-makes-the-faces-se.lay: The framework's account of a particle family builds it from two internal ingredients called slots. Its standing assumption about how a family's states are organised already allows exactly two slots per particle, never three. This result shows that the old idea of the three families as the three pairs chosen from one three-slot object fails that assumption even when only one pair is looked at. In the shared space every particle would appear twice, and the left-right asymmetry of the weak force would cancel out. This adds to an earlier result that the families must be three separate objects. The same assumption, and the requirement that the theory be free of anomalies, are satisfied by any number of separate families, which is standard. If the strengths of both nuclear-type forces are to weaken at high energy, at most five families are allowed. That there are three is not derived: it is only a reading that rests on a separate, observation-level bound that the largest object has three slots, which can be paired in three ways.

proofs.main:
\emph{(1).} This restates clause (G) of the premise, which says the one-slot space is a single doublet; we give the representation-theoretic form. Under clause (a) of Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}, which is the setting of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}, $F$ is a finite-dimensional polynomial representation of $U(2)$ graded so that $\mu I_{2}$ acts on $F_{n}$ as $\mu^{n}$. A polynomial representation is a sum of polynomial irreducibles (complete reducibility), and these are labelled by highest weights $(\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2})$, $\lambda_{1} \ge \lambda_{2} \ge 0$, with torus weights $(p, q)$, $p + q = \lambda_{1} + \lambda_{2}$, running over $q = \lambda_{2}, \dots, \lambda_{1}$, so of dimension $\lambda_{1} - \lambda_{2} + 1$, and with $\mu I_{2}$ acting as $\mu^{\lambda_{1} + \lambda_{2}}$ (standard). On $F_{1}$ the degree is one, so every irreducible summand is $(1, 0)$, the doublet, of dimension two: $\dim F_{1}$ is even. If $F$ is generated in the sense of (G), as in that theorem, $\dim F_{0} = 1$ and an equivariant map $\C^{2} \otimes F_{0} \to F_{1}$ is onto, so $\dim F_{1} \le 2$, and $F_{1}$ is the doublet or zero (with CPT closure, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) gives $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$, so the doublet). A three-dimensional one-slot space is excluded whatever the action of $U(2)$. The script enumerates the irreducibles of degree $0$ to $4$ with their weights and dimensions and confirms that degree one has only dimension two.

\emph{(2).} Take the face $F$ with remaining slot $s_{o}$, the gauge group acting by $U(2)$ on $S_{F}$, trivially on $s_{o}$, and by $U(3)$ on $W$. If the slot number counts all three slots, the state $s_{o}$ has $n = 1$ while $\mu I_{2}$ acts on it as $1 = \mu^{0}$, which clause (a) forbids; the same holds on the $32$ monomials containing $s_{o}$. If the slot number counts only the face's slots, then $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}S_{F} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C s_{o})$ and $F_{0} = \mathrm{span}\{1, s_{o}\}$, against $\dim F_{0} = 1$; the map $x \mapsto s_{o} \wedge x$ is an injective equivariant map from the monomials without $s_{o}$ onto those with it, so every weight (weak $T_{3}$, face slot number, colour occupation) occurs exactly twice. This is the signature the premise names in its refutation condition: more than one slot vacuum, showing itself as two copies of each species. The parity of the total mode number differs between $x$ and $s_{o} \wedge x$, so the even half consists of the face's even states (its particle half) and the images of its odd states, which carry the weights of its antiparticle half: a generation together with its conjugate, a vectorlike pair. The script checks all of this for each of the three faces on the $64$ exterior states, including the rank $16$ of the image of the odd face states under $x \mapsto s_{o} \wedge x$ (GA's exterior model). Now let one gauge group act. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}(1), at most one face plane is an irreducible invariant subspace for any algebra acting on the slots, so at most one face's states form a slot module for that group, and by the above the shared space does not either. If each of three generations is to be a composite satisfying the premise for the one gauge group, the three state spaces are therefore three separate slot modules $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W_{F})$, each with its own slots and, by clause (a) (one pair system per composite), its own pair modes; the faces of Theorem \claimref{families.three-identical-families-mixing-shared-slots} enter only as labels. This is the conclusion of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.faces-of-one-slot-space-are-not-three-generations-under-one-gauge-group}(3), reached there through the overlap counts and the gauge-group lemma; the present step adds that the shared space fails the premise for one face already, through the premise's own refutation signature.

\emph{(3).} Every clause of the premise speaks of one composite's state space; a set of $n$ separate composites satisfies it composite by composite. The particle half of one slot module (chirality $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$, the even part, by the premise's derivation) has the $16$ states $(n, k) = (0,0), (0,2), (1,1), (1,3), (2,0), (2,2)$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, \tfrac16, -\tfrac12, 1, \tfrac13$ and multiplicities $1, 3, 6, 2, 1, 3$. The four conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} are sums over states that are linear in the content: $\sum Y$, $\sum Y^{3}$, $\sum Y T_{3}^{2}$ (weak), $\sum Y h^{2}$ (colour, $h$ a colour Cartan generator), and the colour cubic $\sum h_{8}^{3}$; each vanishes for one copy (the script computes them exactly from the states) and so equals $n \cdot 0$ for $n$ copies. A copy has four weak doublets (three colours of the quark doublet and the lepton doublet), so $n$ copies have $4n$, an even number for every $n$, which is the condition of Witten's global $SU(2)$ anomaly (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-witten-global-su2-anomaly}). Nothing in the premise or in anomaly freedom refers to $n$, so they hold for every $n \ge 1$, and the number of generations is independent of them. This is standard per-generation anomaly cancellation, read as an independence statement. The script checks $n = 1, \dots, 10$ and that the wrong normalisation $Y = (3n - k)/6$ is anomalous.

\emph{(4).} Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}(4), under its Krein premise (\claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}), gives $b_{3} = -11 + \tfrac23\sum T$ and $b_{2} = -\tfrac{22}{3} + \tfrac23\sum T + \tfrac{n_{h}}{6}$ with the Weyl Dynkin sums of the content. Computed from the states, $\sum T_{3}^{2} = 2$ and $\sum h^{2} = 2$ per copy ($h = \mathrm{diag}(\tfrac12, -\tfrac12, 0)$), giving the stored formula. $b_{3} < 0$ exactly when $\tfrac43 n < 11$, $n \le 8$; $b_{2} < 0$ exactly when $\tfrac43 n < \tfrac{22}{3} - \tfrac{n_{h}}{6}$, which for $n_{h} = 1$ and $2$ is $n \le 5$. Both coefficients increase with $n$, so the bounds hold for all $n$; the script checks $n \le 12$. This is the stored condition $8n_{g} + n_{h} < 44$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}(4) at $n_{h} = 1, 2$, standard; it bounds $n$ only if both non-abelian factors are required to be asymptotically free, which no stored result requires of the weak factor.

\emph{(5).} In $\Cl(3,0)$ the grade-four part of $B^{2}$ vanishes for every bivector $B$ (there is no grade four), so $B \wedge B = 0$ and every bivector is a blade, the plane of a face; the coordinate faces $e_{2}e_{3}$, $e_{3}e_{1}$, $e_{1}e_{2}$ span the three bivectors. For $X \in GL(3)$, writing $a \wedge b = I_{3}(a \times b)$, $(Xa) \times (Xb) = \operatorname{cof}(X)(a \times b)$ with $\operatorname{cof}(X) = \det(X)X^{-\mathsf T}$ (standard); so $\Lambda^{2}S \cong S^{*} \otimes \det$. The script verifies the identity on all three faces for two rational matrices, computing the wedges with GA, and that $\operatorname{cof}(X)/\det X$ is the inverse transpose. $\binom{N}{2} = N$ means $N(N - 3) = 0$. So $\Lambda^{2}S$ is the dual triplet of the slot space twisted by the determinant. The reading that the generation labels are the face space is an argued reading under a further hypothesis, not a consequence of (2): separate composites carry no shared slot and need no labels from the maximal composite at all, so taking $\Lambda^{2}S$ as their label space, with the maximal hierarchy's slot $\su(3)$ (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}) acting on it, is a new family-symmetry hypothesis. Under it the count is $3$, and it rests in addition on the three-spinor bound, imported at observation level (Fact \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}). The result is transport-absent: it is representation theory on the slot module.
